item.title: Forget Ravenloft: The Best Horror TTRPG Makes a Party Game Terrifying
item.description: While most tabletop role-playing games are focused on heroic adventure, many incorporate elements of horror to try to keep players on edge. Dungeons & Dragons and Pathfinder offer plenty of creepy monsters, horror-focused settings like Ravenloft and Ustalav, and rules for characters with unsettling powers. Call of Cthulhu and Delta Green make sanity a resource worn down by exposure to the unknown, until characters begin to crack under the stress. Ten Candles evokes fear by literally dimming the lights, while 13 Omens makes dice rolls increasingly perilous as the game goes on.
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson

item.title: Rolfes reveals why Hofmann was chosen over Boniface for Leverkusen's Europa League squad
item.description: Rolfes reveals why Hofmann was chosen over Boniface for Leverkusen's Europa League squad Following Martin Terrier's injury, Bayer Leverkusen have decided to include Jonas Hofmann in their Europa League squad as the Frenchman's replacement. This means Victor Boniface will remain out of the squad for Thursday's Europa League clash against OFI, with Bayer Leverkusen managing director for sport Simon Rolfes explaining the decision ahead of the team's departure for Crete. “Jonas is a very versatile player who can play in different positions. I think it's important to have different types of players available for different situations. If we could have, we would have liked to take both, but we decided on Jonas, and he will be with us tomorrow,” Rolfes said, according to Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger. Boniface played a key role in Leverkusen's success under Xabi Alonso, helping Die Werkself secure the domestic double. However, recurring injuries, particularly knee problems, have hampered his progress since then. So far this season, the Nigerian forward has been limited to just five minutes of action this season, but Rolfes believes his opportunity will come. “This doesn't change Boni's situation. He needs to stay fit, keep working hard and continue improving, and then his opportunity will come. I'm not worried. His most difficult situation came in early summer, and he has worked his way out of it. Since then, he has been in a much better place, mentally as well, and can once again see many more opportunities ahead of him,” the Leverkusen chief said. “In terms of intensity, pressing and working against the ball were never his main strengths, even when he was playing and scoring goals. He has other qualities. We want to get his fitness level as high as possible so that he can showcase his undoubted abilities even more effectively.”

item.title: RFEF confirms four-match suspension for Real Betis midfielder after clash with Lamine Yamal
item.description: RFEF confirms four-match suspension for Real Betis midfielder after clash with Lamine Yamal Real Betis midfielder Facundo Bernal has been handed a four-match suspension following his confrontation with Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal, with the RFEF Disciplinary Committee ruling that the incident constituted an assault under Spanish football’s disciplinary regulations. As reported by Mundo Deportivo , the punishment follows Bernal’s red card during Betis’ meeting with Barcelona last Saturday. The midfielder was dismissed after an altercation with Yamal, who intervened when tensions escalated around teammate Fermin Lopez. RFEF explains why Bernal received a four-match suspension The disciplinary committee based its decision on the referee’s account of the incident and Article 103 of the Disciplinary Code, which covers assaults committed without causing injury. Ricardo de Burgos Bengoechea’s report described the sequence that led to Bernal’s dismissal in the 54th minute, making clear that the confrontation involved physical contact while the ball was out of play. “In the 54th minute, player (6) FACUNDO BERNAL CRUZ was sent off for the following reason: during a confrontation, this player grabbed an opponent by the neck and headbutted him twice in quick succession in the face, whilst the ball was not in play. “The opposing player did not require medical attention and was able to continue the match,” the referee’s report stated Notably, Article 103 provides for a suspension of four to twelve matches when a player assaults another person without causing injury, with the fact that play has stopped serving as a determining factor in establishing intent. Bernal has received the minimum four-match punishment under that provision. How the confrontation with Lamine Yamal unfolded The incident began shortly after half-time, when Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles attempted to help Fermin Lopez up while the Barcelona midfielder was on the ground. Yamal stepped in to support his teammate, bringing him into a confrontation with Bernal. Facundo Bernal has been given a four-match ban. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) The Betis midfielder first grabbed Yamal before the exchange escalated into a clash of heads. The referee subsequently showed Bernal a straight red card, leaving Betis to continue without him. The disciplinary ruling therefore addresses not simply a heated exchange between opponents, but an incident that the referee explicitly described as involving two headbutts while the ball was out of play. Barcelona extended their lead after the red card Bernal was dismissed with Barcelona leading 3-2, but the match moved further in the visitors’ favour after the sending-off. Barça eventually secured a 5-2 victory, turning a closely contested encounter into a more convincing result. item.title: Opponent watch: Barcelona midfielder out of Real Madrid clash through injury
item.description: Opponent watch: Barcelona midfielder out of Real Madrid clash through injury Ahead of the weekend blockbuster encounter at the Spotify Camp Nou against Real Madrid, FC Barcelona have suffered a major injury setback. According to Carlos Monfort of SPORT , the Blaugrana have lost attacking midfielder Dani Olmo to an adductor tear with the Spanish international now set to miss the first El Clasico of the 2026/27 season. Olmo injured Olmo suffered the injury during Barcelona’s 4-2 loss to Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday night. The 2026 FIFA World Cup winner was part of the starting XI for Barça at Parc des Princes, but lasted only 27 minutes as he suffered a muscle injury following a collision with Vitinha. Olmo is injured. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) After being assessed by the medical staff, he was withdrawn by manager Hansi Flick, with Fermin Lopez replacing him on the field. Now, following tests conducted earlier today, it has been confirmed that Olmo has suffered an adductor tear, which will rule him out of action for four weeks. As such, he will be unavailable to face Real Madrid at the Spotify Camp Nou this Sunday in La Liga. Another blow for Barcelona This comes as the latest in a series of injury concerns for Barcelona leading up to the heavyweight clash against Real Madrid. The current La Liga leaders already lost both Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde to injuries this past weekend during their game against Real Betis. Dani Olmo will miss the Clasico . (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Their availability for the first Clasico of the season remains uncertain, with now Olmo also joining them on the sidelines. Andreas Christensen, too, is unavailable with an injury, while Roony Bardghji is a long-term absentee. Along with the injuries, the Blaugrana have suffered their first defeat of the season against PSG, leaving them in a vulnerable position ahead of the weekend’s heavyweight clash. This situation could present Real Madrid with a great opportunity to capitalise on and come away with all three points from Catalonia this weekend. As things stand, Jose Mourinho & co. are third in the La Liga standings, six points behind their arch-rivals, and one below second-placed Atletico Madrid.

item.title: 2026 AMAA Nominations: Slum Bomber, One Woman, One Bra & To Adaego With Love Lead the Pack
item.description: To Adaego With Love leads Nigerian nominations for the 2026 Africa Movie Academy Awards. Photo Credit: Nwamaka Chikezie/Instagram The nominations for the 22nd Africa Movie Academy Awards (AMAA) are out, and there’s already plenty to unpack ahead of the ceremony in Lagos this November. From Uganda and Kenya to Nigeria and South Africa, films from across the continent are competing for some of African cinema’s biggest honours. Leading this year’s nominations are Uganda’s Slum Bomber and Kenya’s One Woman , One Bra , with 14 nominations each. Nigeria is also well represented, with Nwamaka Chikezie ‘s To Adaego With Love earning 11 nominations, while Daniel Etim-Effiong ‘s The Herd follows closely with 10. They’re in good company. South Africa’s The Trek and Ben Made It , alongside Côte d’Ivoire’s Colours of Exile , have also received 10 nominations each, while Colours of Fire has nine. The nominees were announced during a livestream on AMAA’s official YouTube channel. Now, attention turns to the awards ceremony on 15 November 2026 at the Lagos Marriott Hotel, where filmmakers, actors and other industry professionals will gather to celebrate the year’s achievements in African cinema. item.title: Jordan Elliott release, explained: Titans player involved in gun incident at team facility
item.description: Jordan Elliott release, explained: Titans player involved in gun incident at team facility originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tennessee Titans are coming off their first win of the season, but the team had a serious situation to handle around the game. The Titans released veteran defensive tackle Jordan Elliott on Tuesday unexpectedly after what the team described as "an incident" at its practice facility. Elliott signed a two-year, $8 million deal with the Titans in the offseason, following head coach Robert Saleh to Tennessee from the San Francisco 49ers . Further reporting on the matter revealed that the incident involving Elliott escalated to the point where the defensive tackle went to get a gun from his car during the workday. While the incident ultimately de-escalated, the Titans decided that it was enough to move on from Elliott in the middle of the season. Here's a breakdown of what happened with Jordan Elliott. MORE : Full timeline of Jalen Hurts' blood clot issues, information Jordan Elliott release The Titans announced on Tuesday that they released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott following an incident involving Elliott last week. “On Thursday, October 15, there was an incident at our team facility involving Jordan Elliott," the team said in a statement . "Following our review of the incident, we have made the decision to release Elliott from our roster. We will have no further comment on the matter." Tennessee did not initially reveal any details about the situation, but Elliott was not active on Sunday for the first time this season. Later in the day, Easton Freeze of A to Z Sports said that Elliott's release happened because he got into an altercation with teammate JC Latham on the practice field on Thursday, after which he went to get a gun from his car before John Franklin-Myers talked him down. MORE: 5 ways Sean McVay has failed the Rams so far in 2026 Why did Jordan Elliott retrieve a gun? The Titans didn't describe the incident between Elliott and Latham upon releasing the defensive tackle, but Elliott had reportedly been dealing with issues away from the facility. Then, in practice on Thursday, Elliott and Latham got into a fight, which resulted in the coaching staff telling Elliott to leave the field. After practice, Elliott apparently went to get a gun from his car before John Franklin-Myers talked him down. "Jordan has been having a lot of problems away from the building and obviously he brought it to work with him," a source told reporter Aaron Wilson . "There was no reason for him to go off like that. Everyone thought that was wild. To overreact like that is absolutely crazy. We're just glad that no one got hurt and it's over." MORE : Full timeline of Jalen Hurts' blood clot issues, information Jordan Elliott release The Titans announced on Tuesday that they released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott following an incident involving Elliott last week. “On Thursday, October 15, there was an incident at our team facility involving Jordan Elliott," the team said in a statement . "Following our review of the incident, we have made the decision to release Elliott from our roster. We will have no further comment on the matter." Tennessee did not initially reveal any details about the situation, but Elliott was not active on Sunday for the first time this season. Later in the day, Easton Freeze of A to Z Sports said that Elliott's release happened because he got into an altercation with teammate JC Latham on the practice field on Thursday, after which he went to get a gun from his car before John Franklin-Myers talked him down. MORE: 5 ways Sean McVay has failed the Rams so far in 2026 Why did Jordan Elliott retrieve a gun? The Titans didn't describe the incident between Elliott and Latham upon releasing the defensive tackle, but Elliott had reportedly been dealing with issues away from the facility. Then, in practice on Thursday, Elliott and Latham got into a fight, which resulted in the coaching staff telling Elliott to leave the field. After practice, Elliott apparently went to get a gun from his car before John Franklin-Myers talked him down. "Jordan has been having a lot of problems away from the building and obviously he brought it to work with him," a source told reporter Aaron Wilson . "There was no reason for him to go off like that. Everyone thought that was wild. To overreact like that is absolutely crazy. We're just glad that no one got hurt and it's over." item.title: 2027: Sowore’s AAC writes Tinubu, demands presidential villa for campaign council inauguration
item.description: By Emmanuel Okogba The African Action Congress (AAC) has formally requested approval from President Bola Tinubu to hold the inauguration of its Presidential Campaign Council at the Presidential Villa in Aso Rock, Abuja, and has asked for logistical support for 5,000 participants. In a letter dated 21 October 2026 and signed by National Secretary Oshiokhue Philip Ikpeminoghena, the party said it wants to stage the ceremony on 11 November 2026 “in preparation for the 2027 general elections.” The AAC also requested the provision of food, drinks and other logistical support for the 5,000 expected attendees from within Nigeria and abroad. The party said the request was made “consistent with the arrangements reportedly extended to the All Progressives Congress (APC) for a similar political engagement.” “In the spirit of multiparty democracy, political inclusiveness, and equal treatment of political parties,” the letter stated, granting the request would demonstrate the Presidency’s commitment to fairness, equal access, and the principle that public institutions must serve all Nigerians without partisan discrimination. The AAC said it looks forward to a favourable response and asked for information on the applicable procedures and conditions for approval. The letter was addressed to the President and Commander-in-Chief at the Presidential Villa, Aso Rock, Abuja. Vanguard reports that Omoyele Sowore is the AAC’s candidate for next year’s election The post 2027: Sowore’s AAC writes Tinubu, demands presidential villa for campaign council inauguration appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Schottenheimer wants to stop making mistakes, but it's more than that
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys had to go into their boogie man's house and fell short across the board, losing 23-13 to the Green Bay Packers . No part of the team played well in the first half, falling down 17-0, with the offense having two turnovers and the defense allowing a 90% conversion rate on third down. The team was lucky the Packers dropped multiple touchdown passes, keeping the game competitive. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said the effort was right, but the team needs to eliminate mistakes; the issues seem much deeper than on-field mistakes. The offense didn’t bounce back in the second half. Green Bay offered very little offensively in the third and fourth quarters, but Dallas couldn’t do anything to make the game close . They had their offensive line intact, the three main receivers were healthy, Dak Prescott was under center, Javonte Williams was a full go at running back, and Brevyn Spann-Ford replaced a healthy Jake Ferguson at tight end. With all that at their disposal, Dallas had a single score while the game was in the balance. It was an unacceptable performance from that side of the ball, and putting it all on "mistakes" isn't good enough. Third down is the main issue with the Dallas defense It’s not difficult to figure out the issue with the Dallas defense. They allowed 17 points in the first half and it could’ve been more if not for self-inflicted mistakes by the Packers. The Cowboys allowed four third-down conversions on the opening drive. Two from third-and-13, a third-and-5 and a touchdown on third-and-six. They ended the half allowing 9 of 10 third-down conversions, and for the second time in just six games this season. This allowed GB to run 39 plays to the Cowboys' 23 and control the clock 17 minutes to 13, while the Packers only rushed for 2.7 yards per carry in the opening two quarters. In the second half, the defense turned things around as Green Bay only scored six points on five possessions. They allowed only two conversions on eight attempts and held the Packers under 30 plays before kneel-downs, with 13 minutes of time of possession. When they get off the field, the defense looks okay, but when opponents can extend drives on third down, they look abysmal. The coaches need to look at how they are using their personnel. Von Miller covering the flat or Malachi Lawrence covering an in-route 20 yards downfield, in the end zone instead of rushing the passer, isn't going to be impactful often. The Cowboys are struggling versus the blitz Dallas played a Tampa Bay Buccaneers defense under Todd Bowles that blitzed often, and it badly impacted the quarterback and the offense overall. It was a short week, and the Cowboys were at the end of a tough travel schedule, but those reasons weren’t available for the matchup with the Packers. Dallas had a mini bye to prepare for another defensive coordinator who blitzes and plays Prescott well, Jonathan Gannon. It was a short week, and the Cowboys were at the end of a tough travel schedule, but those reasons weren’t available for the matchup with the Packers. Dallas had a mini bye to prepare for another defensive coordinator who blitzes and plays Prescott well, Jonathan Gannon. While the head coach for the Arizona Cardinals, Gannon was 3-0 and held the Cowboys to 22, 17, and 16 points. The fact that Brian Schottenheimer seemed to have no plan to counter Green Bay’s defense is not promising for the season's future. The players made mistakes. Prescott missed throws, and the offensive line played poorly, but a lot of that could be due to a lack of a game plan to counter the blitz. Brian Schottenheimer is running out of excuses The Joneses have been the guys taking the brunt of criticism for 30 years without success, and rightfully so, but at the micro level, Brian Schottenheimer has been an issue in his first 23 games. The team has had poor defense and special teams play under his watch, but now his unit on offense has been poor over the last two games. The offense played the last two contests fully healthy, so there are no excuses for why they aren't thriving. Instead, they are falling apart. Over the last two contests, Dallas is 12-for-26 on third down, has turned the ball over five times, and has only scored 14.5 points per game. The offense has been the furthest from the greatest offense there is, and with a completely healthy unit, the blame will fall at the play-caller's feet. Schottenheimer is coaching for his job now. item.title: Today in Motorsport History, October 21: Räikkönen Wins the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix and the F1 Title by One Point
item.description: Ferrari has not produced a Formula 1 drivers’ champion since Kimi Räikkönen at the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix. File image from Melbourne. Photo: Ken So / Unsplash Kimi Räikkönen started the last race of 2007 third in the standings, seven points behind a rookie and three behind a two-time champion. By the end of the afternoon he was the Formula 1 world champion. Räikkönen won the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos on October 21, 2007, 19 years ago today. Lewis Hamilton’s McLaren suffered a gearbox glitch early, and Ferrari ran a one-two that put Räikkönen’s 110 points one clear of both McLaren drivers on 109. It was the first time since 1986 that three drivers had arrived at a season finale with a chance at the title. It is also the last time a Ferrari driver has won it. Seventeen points down with two races to go The 2007 season belonged to McLaren for most of its length, and so did the trouble. Hamilton, in his debut season, and Fernando Alonso, who had just won back-to-back titles with Renault, spent the year taking points off each other in identical cars. Meanwhile, the espionage case involving Ferrari technical data ended with McLaren excluded from the constructors’ championship. Räikkönen, in his first year at Ferrari after replacing Michael Schumacher, looked out of it with two races left. He was 17 points behind Hamilton. However, Hamilton scored nothing in China while Räikkönen won there, his fifth victory of the season. As a result, Hamilton went to Brazil on 107 points, Alonso on 103 and Räikkönen on 100. What each driver needed at the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix Under the 10-8-6-5-4-3-2-1 points system, Hamilton controlled the title. A fifth-place finish would have been enough whatever his rivals did. Alonso had to recover a four-point gap to his teammate while also keeping Räikkönen behind him. Räikkönen’s path was the narrowest. He needed to win, with Alonso no higher than third and Hamilton no higher than sixth. A sixth place for Hamilton would have tied them on 110, but Räikkönen would have taken the title on wins. In other words, the Finn needed his own perfect day and a bad one for both McLarens. Hamilton (107): fifth or better and the title was his. Alonso (103): needed a strong finish, ideally a win or second place, and help from Hamilton’s result. Räikkönen (100): win, Alonso third or lower, Hamilton sixth or lower. item.content:encoded: Ferrari has not produced a Formula 1 drivers’ champion since Kimi Räikkönen at the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix. File image from Melbourne. Photo: Ken So / Unsplash Kimi Räikkönen started the last race of 2007 third in the standings, seven points behind a rookie and three behind a two-time champion. By the end of the afternoon he was the Formula 1 world champion. Räikkönen won the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos on October 21, 2007, 19 years ago today. Lewis Hamilton’s McLaren suffered a gearbox glitch early, and Ferrari ran a one-two that put Räikkönen’s 110 points one clear of both McLaren drivers on 109. It was the first time since 1986 that three drivers had arrived at a season finale with a chance at the title. It is also the last time a Ferrari driver has won it. Seventeen points down with two races to go The 2007 season belonged to McLaren for most of its length, and so did the trouble. Hamilton, in his debut season, and Fernando Alonso, who had just won back-to-back titles with Renault, spent the year taking points off each other in identical cars. Meanwhile, the espionage case involving Ferrari technical data ended with McLaren excluded from the constructors’ championship. Räikkönen, in his first year at Ferrari after replacing Michael Schumacher, looked out of it with two races left. He was 17 points behind Hamilton. However, Hamilton scored nothing in China while Räikkönen won there, his fifth victory of the season. As a result, Hamilton went to Brazil on 107 points, Alonso on 103 and Räikkönen on 100. What each driver needed at the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix Under the 10-8-6-5-4-3-2-1 points system, Hamilton controlled the title. A fifth-place finish would have been enough whatever his rivals did. Alonso had to recover a four-point gap to his teammate while also keeping Räikkönen behind him. Räikkönen’s path was the narrowest. He needed to win, with Alonso no higher than third and Hamilton no higher than sixth. A sixth place for Hamilton would have tied them on 110, but Räikkönen would have taken the title on wins. In other words, the Finn needed his own perfect day and a bad one for both McLarens. Hamilton (107): fifth or better and the title was his. Alonso (103): needed a strong finish, ideally a win or second place, and help from Hamilton’s result. Räikkönen (100): win, Alonso third or lower, Hamilton sixth or lower. Lap one and a gearbox glitch Felipe Massa took pole at his home race, and Hamilton started alongside him. Räikkönen started third and Alonso fourth. At the start, Massa squeezed Hamilton, Räikkönen went around the outside into second, and Alonso passed Hamilton for third. Then Hamilton tried to retake the place down the hill into Turn 4, locked up, ran wide and rejoined eighth. Eighth was still recoverable. What came next was not. A few laps later Hamilton’s McLaren slowed sharply with an electronic gearbox problem, and by the time the car came back to life he had dropped to 18th. He spent the rest of the afternoon climbing back through the field on a three-stop strategy, but he could not get higher than seventh. Fans on the terraces at Interlagos, where three drivers arrived with a shot at the 2007 title. File image from the 2022 race weekend. Photo: Eduardo Taulois / Unsplash How Ferrari swapped its leaders in the pits With Hamilton out of the picture, the title came down to the order of the two Ferraris. Massa led, Räikkönen sat behind him, and Alonso ran a distant third. If the race finished that way, Hamilton would keep the crown. Ferrari settled it with fuel and timing rather than team orders on track. Both cars made their first stops on lap 21. For the second round, Massa pitted from the lead on lap 50. Räikkönen stayed out until lap 53 and used the light-fuel laps to build enough time to rejoin ahead. When the stops shook out, Räikkönen led Massa, and the championship order flipped. Räikkönen won by 1.493 seconds. Massa finished second, and Alonso was third, 57 seconds back. Hamilton crossed the line seventh. Pit-stop timing decided the lead at Interlagos in 2007, when Räikkönen stayed out three laps longer than Massa. File image from 2022. Photo: Eduardo Taulois / Unsplash One point, and a protest that changed nothing The final table read Räikkönen 110, Hamilton 109, Alonso 109. Hamilton took second on countback. Räikkönen, who had finished second at Interlagos in each of the previous three years, became Finland’s third world champion after Keke Rosberg and Mika Häkkinen. Afterward he credited a team that, in his words, “always believed we could recover.” Ferrari also took the constructors’ title. There was one more twist. After the race, the FIA technical delegate reported that fuel in the BMW Sauber and Williams cars was more than 10°C below ambient temperature, which the rules did not allow. The stewards declined to penalize them, citing doubt over the true fuel and ambient temperatures. McLaren appealed. Had those cars been excluded, Hamilton would have moved up to fourth and won the title. In November 2007, the FIA International Court of Appeal ruled McLaren’s appeal inadmissible, and the result stood. Why the 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix still matters It is still Ferrari’s last drivers’ title. Massa came within one point at the same circuit a year later. Since then, Ferrari has won races and the 2008 constructors’ championship, but no Ferrari driver has been crowned. Every season that passes makes October 21, 2007, a bigger date in Maranello’s history. Ferrari’s modern title era began with Schumacher ending a 21-year wait at Suzuka in 2000 , and Räikkönen’s title remains its last entry. It shaped Hamilton’s career. The rookie lost the title by one point at Interlagos. Twelve months later, he won it there by one point over Massa, passing Timo Glock on the final lap to take the fifth place he needed. That pairing of results is one reason the circuit carries so much weight in his story. It closed an era of driver aids. Brazil 2007 was the last Grand Prix before the FIA’s standard ECU, supplied by McLaren Electronic Systems, arrived for 2008. The change banned traction control and electronic engine-braking aids, and that put car control back in drivers’ hands. It belongs to a long line of one-point finishes. The 2007 decider sits alongside Mike Hawthorn’s one-point title in 1958 as proof that a championship can turn on a single position. Fittingly, Räikkönen’s 21st and final Grand Prix win came on October 21, 2018, in Austin, 11 years to the day after Interlagos. He retired after the 2021 season with that single world title. Nineteen years on, the lesson from Interlagos still applies to the current fight. As Kimi Antonelli heads to Austin with a chance to seal the 2026 title, the records he could break are a reminder that a lead is never final until the math says so. item.title: Frankie Muniz offers new details on 2027 NASCAR plans
item.description: Motorsport photo Actor-turned-racer Frankie Muniz has had an interesting 2026 season. He has missed a handful of NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series races where he was meant to compete full-time for Reaume in the No. 33 Ford, but he had a pretty good reason. Muniz was also busy chasing a GT4 America title, which he achieved with co-driver Tyler Stone in the Am Class after a three-win season. Driving the TechSport Racing Ford Mustang, he earned his first professional racing title after a journey that began twenty years ago. But with his recent success in sports car racing, will we see less of Muniz in NASCAR going forward? Frankie Muniz, Team Reaume Frankie Muniz, Team Reaume “It’s been an amazing journey," said Muniz in a Tuesday media availability. "When I do something, I do it fully. People always ask me what my hobbies are, I don’t have hobbies. When I do something, I want to do it at the highest level I can possibly do it and try to be the best. I still feel like I have a lot of unfinished business in the racing world, especially in the NASCAR world. It’s such a tough series. It’s such a tough sport. There are so many good drivers, so many good teams, and I feel like I’ve figured out a lot. I feel like I’m a much better racer and driver than I was when I came in, but I’m still not necessarily seeing the results that I expect to see or want to see. "So, that’s why I’m not finished yet in the NASCAR world. Like I said earlier, I have an amazing relationship with Ford and I’m so grateful to have an amazing manufacturer supporting my racing journey, and they pushed me this year to give the sportscar world a try because they have the Mustang Challenge Series, the GT4 car, the GT3 car. They have the Hypercar coming out. They’re really putting an emphasis on their sportscar program and I went over there not knowing what to expect and won the championship and won a bunch of races. That felt incredible. That’s not something I’ve ever done in my racing career, like to really kind of be there and feel like you can win, and it feels really good. I’m not gonna lie. That said, I am not finished in the NASCAR world." Muniz noted that he is taking "guidance from a bunch of places" as he works on the next steps of his career, but again asserted that he "will be racing NASCAR ... As of right now, it’s not necessarily full-time, but it’s not that it won’t be. There’s a lot of moving pieces as always when it comes to everybody’s schedule in the racing world, and we’re ironing it out. I love Josh (Reaume). I love my team and if I’m back in the NASCAR world, it will be with them again, but I know we want to prove what we’ve been working on even more, so we’ll do that, whether it be a part-time basis or full-time, I will be in the NASCAR Truck Series next year in some capacity.” Muniz embarked on a career in stock car racing with ARCA in 2023, later making starts in the NASCAR O'Reilly Series and even becoming a full-time driver in the NASCAR Truck Series. item.title: AI cuts coding time, but it's also filling open source's inbox with crap
item.description: Generative AI is saving open source developers time while giving maintainers more rubbish to sift through, according to a Linux Foundation survey. Respondents estimated that a quarter of incoming pull requests – proposed code changes – were low-quality "AI slop." Open source projects have spent the past year grappling with AI-generated contributions, useful vulnerability discoveries, false positives, and duplicate reports. Linus Torvalds has warmed to the tools , while remaining critical of low-quality submissions. The foundation argues that projects need clearer policies and better tools to handle the influx. Almost three-quarters (71 percent) of maintainers reckon GenAI has lowered the barriers to contributing to open source, but just over half (53 percent) disagree that the technology has improved community trust. Respondents estimated that AI cut code-authoring time by 52 percent on average. But for highly complex tasks, 21 percent reported taking longer. Then there is governance. Only 35 percent of projects have a formal policy permitting GenAI use, while 32 percent have no policy and no plans for one, leaving expectations unclear across much of the community. Hilary Carter, SVP of Research at the Linux Foundation, said: "Open source projects need to design for a growing AI-generated contributor base, not simply react to it. That means setting clear expectations for GenAI, putting responsibility for testing and disclosure on contributors and giving maintainers better tools to manage incoming pull requests." Among large projects, the estimated share of incoming pull requests classified as AI slop rises to 31 percent. The workload extends beyond proposed code changes. The curl project announced this week it will move low and medium severity severity flaws to public view to protect a security team almost overwhelmed by AI-assisted reports. Project maintainer Daniel Stenberg said : "We are struggling as a project as all key maintainers feel strained, overloaded and brought to the brink of what we can muster." On the need for better tools for maintainers, Carter said: "If we get those fundamentals right, AI can expand participation without overburdening and increasing costs for maintainers." ®

item.content:encoded: Generative AI is saving open source developers time while giving maintainers more rubbish to sift through, according to a Linux Foundation survey. Respondents estimated that a quarter of incoming pull requests – proposed code changes – were low-quality "AI slop." Open source projects have spent the past year grappling with AI-generated contributions, useful vulnerability discoveries, false positives, and duplicate reports. Linus Torvalds has warmed to the tools , while remaining critical of low-quality submissions. The foundation argues that projects need clearer policies and better tools to handle the influx. Almost three-quarters (71 percent) of maintainers reckon GenAI has lowered the barriers to contributing to open source, but just over half (53 percent) disagree that the technology has improved community trust. Respondents estimated that AI cut code-authoring time by 52 percent on average. But for highly complex tasks, 21 percent reported taking longer. Then there is governance. Only 35 percent of projects have a formal policy permitting GenAI use, while 32 percent have no policy and no plans for one, leaving expectations unclear across much of the community. Hilary Carter, SVP of Research at the Linux Foundation, said: "Open source projects need to design for a growing AI-generated contributor base, not simply react to it. That means setting clear expectations for GenAI, putting responsibility for testing and disclosure on contributors and giving maintainers better tools to manage incoming pull requests." Among large projects, the estimated share of incoming pull requests classified as AI slop rises to 31 percent. The workload extends beyond proposed code changes. The curl project announced this week it will move low and medium severity severity flaws to public view to protect a security team almost overwhelmed by AI-assisted reports. Project maintainer Daniel Stenberg said : "We are struggling as a project as all key maintainers feel strained, overloaded and brought to the brink of what we can muster." On the need for better tools for maintainers, Carter said: "If we get those fundamentals right, AI can expand participation without overburdening and increasing costs for maintainers." ®

item.title: A Record-Breaking NASCAR Espionage Case: JGR’s $150 Million Fight With Spire
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Joe Gibbs Racing is seeking nearly $150 million in damages from Spire Motorsports and former competition director Chris Gabehart in a lawsuit over alleged trade secret theft. The huge figure, revealed in a recent court filing, raises the stakes in a legal battle that could become one of NASCAR’s most expensive team-versus-team disputes. FOX Sports reporter Bob Pockrass mentioned the figure on Tuesday night, October 20, citing a brief filed by Spire. The filing states that JGR is seeking nearly $150 million in damages, with its experts valuing the alleged trade secrets at $47.4 million. Punitive damages account for much of the difference between that valuation and the total demand. The case is also facing questions over its schedule, with the jury trial currently set to begin on February 1, 2027. Ongoing disputes over documents and expert reports could complicate preparations as both sides work toward that date. In its filing, Spire states that “JGR’s damages expert opines that JGR’s damages are $47.4 million” as far as the worth of the trade secrets. (my guess is when adding punitive damages, get to closer to the $150 million total). https://t.co/3JoLGJZSau — Bob Pockrass (@bobpockrass) October 21, 2026 A $150 Million Claim in a Fight Over Racing Secrets Apr 28, 2024; Dover, Delaware, USA; NASCAR Cup Series driver Denny Hamlin (left) chats with crew chief Chris Gabehart (right) on pit road prior to the Wurth 400 at Dover Motor Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Matthew O’Haren-USA TODAY Sports JGR filed the lawsuit in February 2026 after Gabehart left his role as the team’s competition director and joined Spire as chief motorsports officer. Gabehart previously served as Denny Hamlin ’s crew chief and held a senior position overseeing JGR’s competition operations. His move to a rival team became the focus of a dispute over confidential information and the limits of competition between NASCAR organizations. JGR alleges that Gabehart took proprietary information before leaving, including car setups, race-outcome spreadsheets, vacuum-testing procedures, transaxle specifications and airbox-sealing processes. The team claims these materials contain valuable technical knowledge that could give a competitor an advantage. Spire and Gabehart deny the allegations. They argue that the presence of information on personal devices does not prove it was shared with Spire or used to improve the team’s performance. The defense has also pointed to forensic examinations that it says found no evidence that the data was transferred or used by Spire. The court will ultimately have to determine whether JGR can prove its claims and establish that it is entitled to damages. The huge figure, revealed in a recent court filing, raises the stakes in a legal battle that could become one of NASCAR’s most expensive team-versus-team disputes. FOX Sports reporter Bob Pockrass mentioned the figure on Tuesday night, October 20, citing a brief filed by Spire. The filing states that JGR is seeking nearly $150 million in damages, with its experts valuing the alleged trade secrets at $47.4 million. Punitive damages account for much of the difference between that valuation and the total demand. The case is also facing questions over its schedule, with the jury trial currently set to begin on February 1, 2027. Ongoing disputes over documents and expert reports could complicate preparations as both sides work toward that date. In its filing, Spire states that “JGR’s damages expert opines that JGR’s damages are $47.4 million” as far as the worth of the trade secrets. (my guess is when adding punitive damages, get to closer to the $150 million total). https://t.co/3JoLGJZSau — Bob Pockrass (@bobpockrass) October 21, 2026 A $150 Million Claim in a Fight Over Racing Secrets Apr 28, 2024; Dover, Delaware, USA; NASCAR Cup Series driver Denny Hamlin (left) chats with crew chief Chris Gabehart (right) on pit road prior to the Wurth 400 at Dover Motor Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Matthew O’Haren-USA TODAY Sports JGR filed the lawsuit in February 2026 after Gabehart left his role as the team’s competition director and joined Spire as chief motorsports officer. Gabehart previously served as Denny Hamlin ’s crew chief and held a senior position overseeing JGR’s competition operations. His move to a rival team became the focus of a dispute over confidential information and the limits of competition between NASCAR organizations. JGR alleges that Gabehart took proprietary information before leaving, including car setups, race-outcome spreadsheets, vacuum-testing procedures, transaxle specifications and airbox-sealing processes. The team claims these materials contain valuable technical knowledge that could give a competitor an advantage. Spire and Gabehart deny the allegations. They argue that the presence of information on personal devices does not prove it was shared with Spire or used to improve the team’s performance. The defense has also pointed to forensic examinations that it says found no evidence that the data was transferred or used by Spire. The court will ultimately have to determine whether JGR can prove its claims and establish that it is entitled to damages. Also Read: What Happened on Day One of Court in JGR vs. Chris Gabehart and Spire? Could This Be NASCAR’s Costliest Team Espionage Case? The nearly $150 million demand stands out because of the amount involved in a lawsuit between two racing teams. JGR initially sought more than $8 million in damages when it filed the case. The much larger figure now puts the financial stakes on a different scale, with the latest reporting describing the claim as unusually large for a team-versus-team dispute. Although lawsuits involving NASCAR ’s wider corporate structure have involved substantial financial stakes, this case is different: JGR is pursuing another team and a former executive over alleged trade secret misappropriation. A judgment approaching $150 million could have a major financial impact on an independent organization such as Spire. Why the Damages Could Reach Nearly $150 Million According to the figures cited by Pockrass , JGR’s damages experts valued the alleged trade secrets at $47.4 million. The overall demand rises to nearly $150 million when punitive damages are included. Punitive damages may be awarded in certain cases to punish wrongful conduct and discourage similar behavior. They are not automatic, and their availability and amount depend on the applicable law and evidence. The distinction is important because the $47.4 million valuation does not mean a court has found that JGR suffered losses of that amount. Nor does the nearly $150 million demand establish what Spire or Gabehart might ultimately have to pay. The damages issue is likely to be a major part of the case if it reaches trial, particularly as the two sides continue to dispute whether JGR’s confidential information was misappropriated and whether it benefited Spire. item.title: Third time this century - how Australia's stark collapse unfolded
item.description: 99 is Australia's lowest score in Tests since being bowled out for 91 by India in Nagpur in 2023 [Getty Images] Second Test, Gqeberha (day four of five) South Africa 425-9 dec: Bavuma 179, Jansen 85; Boland 5-81 Australia 99: Smith 28; Jansen 5-33 Australia trail by 422 runs Scorecard Australia were forced to follow-on for only the third time in the past 38 years after being dismissed for 99 by South Africa on day four of the second Test in Gqeberha. Left-armer Marco Jansen took a superb 5-33 and Kagiso Rabada and Wiaan Mulder two wickets each as the Proteas roared back into the Test to give them a real shot at leveling the series. They were 110-6 early on day three, their hopes severely dented, but scrapped to 425-9 after Temba Bavuma's 179 and now take a 326-run first innings lead. Australia's surrender was stark. After opener Nic Maddinson was dismissed late on day three, South Africa took the remaining nine wickets inside 40 overs on the fourth day. Steve Smith was the tourists highest scoring with 28. No other batter passed 14 and the highest partnership was just 23. The last time Australia were forced to follow-on was against India at Sydney in 2019. Before that, the most recent previous occasion was the fourth Ashes Test at Trent Bridge in 2005. It was also the biggest first-innings deficit they conceded since a Test against West Indies in November 1984. How Australia's collapse unfolded Jansen sparked the collapse by nicking off nightwatchman Scott Boland with his first ball of the day at the start of the second over. Four overs later he pinned Travis Head lbw on review for 14 and Marnus Labuschagne was brilliantly caught at slip by Simon Harmer off the bowling of Anrich Nortje for the same score. Nortje was only able to bowl 3.3 overs because of an apparent groin issue, which will impact the remainder of the Test if he is unable to bowl again. After Jansen found the edge of Matt Renshaw and Alex Carey in the same over, he also had Beau Webster caught in similar fashion for his fifth Test five-wicket haul. Mitchell Starc and Australia captain Pat Cummins followed within 11 balls of Mulder bowling Smith, who had been given treatment to his neck throughout his 88 balls, and, after a brief conversation with his bowlers, captain Bavuma signaled to Australia's dressing room that they would have to bat again. South Africa now have more than 150 overs to complete victory. Notifications, social media and more with BBC Sport

item.title: Problem or Solution: Jarren Duran
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are stuck. If you’re the type of person who is content finishing third within the division and being bounced by your arch rivals in just a handful of games in back-to-back seasons, you might disagree. If you’re not an idiot, you know difficult decisions need to be made and that things need to change. I’ve decided to task myself with analyzing which players can be part of the turnaround and which should be shown the door, all as a way to take the heat off chief baseball officer Craig Breslow. If you’re not down with that, I’ve got two words for ya: Problem or Solution? Jarren Duran It’s time to rip the band-aid off and talk about the most polarizing player in the organization… Jarren Duran has not-so-slowly devolved from being the heart and soul of the team to dead weight, doing it within three seasons. I’ll go ahead and lay out the numbers for you below, which illustrate just part of the reason we’re even having this conversation… 2024: .285/.342/.492, 21 HR, 75 RBI, 48 2B, 14 3B, 34 SB, 132 OPS+ 2025: .256/.332/.442, 16 HR, 84 RBI, 41 2B, 13 3B, 24 SB, 114 OPS+ 2026: .208/.207/.361, 20 HR, 69 RBI, 15 2B, 5 3B, 21 SB, 76 OPS+ … with the other reason(s) being his penchant for getting into trouble by flipping off fans, using homophobic slurs, threatening to beat up podcasters, and all sorts of other stuff. I’d like to stick to on-field factors, but it’s kind of impossible with this guy in particular. JARREN DURAN JUST STOLE HOME!!!! pic.twitter.com/fcLZx7cgk9 — Red Sox (@RedSox) April 26, 2025 WHAT WE KNOW Duran has worn out his welcome, with all of the things we previously laid out seemingly working together to limit his effectiveness on the field. Duran still showcased an ability to hit for power and cause havoc on the base paths last season, but the consistency was gone and much of that had to do with the fact that he wasn’t entrusted with a full-time role until Roman Anthony was injured on May 4. I’d imagine they aren’t going to suddenly trust him more after the season he just had season, especially with the organization expected to lean on that trio of Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela, and Wilyer Abreu. WHAT WE DON’T KNOW If any of those three players get hurt, which history tells us is just a matter of time, there will be tons of questions surrounding the overall depth of the outfield. Nate Eaton, Jahmai Jones, and Mickey Gasper were getting significant at-bats down the stretch, dude. I don’t have to tell you how bad that is, so while it hurts me to admit, there is at least a track record to look back at with Duran. I’d also like to point out the fact that everything we’ve seen from him over the last two seasons, as well as the impending lockout and an expected uneasiness floating over potential player acquisitions this winter, would tell you that it’s going to be nearly impossible to come to a point where you feel like you’re not getting fleeced in a deal where you send the guy away — so long as he can’t be pawned off on an idiot

I’d like to stick to on-field factors, but it’s kind of impossible with this guy in particular. JARREN DURAN JUST STOLE HOME!!!! pic.twitter.com/fcLZx7cgk9 — Red Sox (@RedSox) April 26, 2025 WHAT WE KNOW Duran has worn out his welcome, with all of the things we previously laid out seemingly working together to limit his effectiveness on the field. Duran still showcased an ability to hit for power and cause havoc on the base paths last season, but the consistency was gone and much of that had to do with the fact that he wasn’t entrusted with a full-time role until Roman Anthony was injured on May 4. I’d imagine they aren’t going to suddenly trust him more after the season he just had season, especially with the organization expected to lean on that trio of Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela, and Wilyer Abreu. WHAT WE DON’T KNOW If any of those three players get hurt, which history tells us is just a matter of time, there will be tons of questions surrounding the overall depth of the outfield. Nate Eaton, Jahmai Jones, and Mickey Gasper were getting significant at-bats down the stretch, dude. I don’t have to tell you how bad that is, so while it hurts me to admit, there is at least a track record to look back at with Duran. I’d also like to point out the fact that everything we’ve seen from him over the last two seasons, as well as the impending lockout and an expected uneasiness floating over potential player acquisitions this winter, would tell you that it’s going to be nearly impossible to come to a point where you feel like you’re not getting fleeced in a deal where you send the guy away — so long as he can’t be pawned off on an idiotic franchise like the San Diego Padres or Philadelphia Phillies. BEST-CASE SCENARIOS San Diego is in desperate need of a spark and mistakenly thinks Duran will provide it, all while thinking its getting a good deal after nearly making a massive mistake with its overly generous offer from two years back . Philadelphia wants another “gritty guy who plays the game the right way” and gives you a lottery ticket to acquire him. WORST-CASE SCENARIO Breslow doesn’t want to get duped, holds onto the asset, and we do this whole song and dance all over again. CONCLUSION It’s addition by subtraction, folks. The Red Sox need to move on from the player and the person — he’s too much of a headache for the production you’ve gotten since the midway point of last season and there’s little reason to expect that he’ll turn things around as he gets older and starts to wear thin.

item.title: Netanyahu’s main election rival rules out serving under him
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s main rival in October 27 elections, ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot, said on Wednesday that he would refuse to serve as a minister in a new government led by the current premier. With the poll just days away, and predictions that no side will win on its own, some commentators have raised the possibility of a unity government convening Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc with centrist and centre-right parties. But speaking to radio station 103 FM on Wednesday, Eisenkot said he was committed, “categorically, to not serving under Netanyahu’s leadership, even within the framework of a rotation” deal in which the two shared power. Eisenkot has campaigned on attacking the fitness to serve of Netanyahu, especially over his failure to prevent the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. Polls show Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition and the opposition camp rallying around Eisenkot are neck and neck, with each projected to win around 50 to 52 seats — just shy of a majority in the 120-member Knesset. In his interview, Eisenkot did not rule out the possibility of a unity government altogether. Former prime minister Naftali Bennet, whose party is polling third, said a government that included the current prime minister would not be an issue for him. It would, however, run counter to Israeli law, which forbids anyone facing charges from serving as a minister — although the bar does not apply for prime minister. Netanyahu is currently on trial and faces several charges of corruption, which he denies. An October 16 poll found that 55 percent of respondents would prefer a unity government over new elections should the upcoming vote fail to produce a clear winner. In 2020, Netanyahu and centrist Benny Gantz set aside their mutual antipathy to strike a power-sharing deal in which they would rotate the prime ministership between them. The agreement followed a period that saw three elections in less than a year, and the resulting government lasted only 13 months. The post Netanyahu’s main election rival rules out serving under him appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gov Otu Presents ₦987.8bn 2027 Budget, Earmarks ₦708.4bn For Capital Projects
item.description: Cross River State Governor, Bassey Otu, on Wednesday presented a proposed ₦987.8 billion budget for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly, christening it the “Budget of Consolidation and Renewed Hope”, reaffirming his administration’s commitment to sustainable development, fiscal discipline and inclusive economic growth. Presenting the estimates in Calabar, Otu described the budget as more than an aggregation of figures, characterising it as “a solemn and sacred pact laden with the trust, expectation and aspiration of the people for their improved livelihoods.” He said its successful implementation would depend on prudent resource management, accountability and disciplined public expenditure, underscoring his administration’s determination to translate its social contract with the people into tangible improvements in their living conditions. The proposed budget, valued at precisely ₦987,808,089,235.92, represents an increase of approximately 2.57 per cent over the 2026 budget. Capital expenditure accounts for ₦708.43 billion, representing 71.72 per cent of the total provision, while recurrent expenditure stands at ₦279.38 billion, or 28.28 per cent. The substantial capital allocation, according to the governor, reflects the government’s determination to prioritise infrastructure, human capital development and productive investments capable of stimulating economic activity. Otu explained that the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework and Fiscal Strategy Paper provided the foundation for the estimates, adding that the budget would sustain ongoing programmes while opening new pathways for investment, employment creation and improved public services. “The imperative of this exercise underscores our collective resolve to chart a sustainable course for the growth and development of our dear State,” he declared. Addressing concerns surrounding the state’s debt profile, the governor maintained that his administration had refrained from obtaining fresh domestic and external loans since assuming office in 2023. Citing verifiable indices from the National Bureau of Statistics and the Debt Management Office, he said Cross River remained among the few states that had not contracted new loans during the period. He attributed the state’s existing debt burden to obligations inherited from previous administrations, explaining that debt servicing had constrained the pace at which available resources could be deployed to development projects. item.content:encoded: Cross River State Governor, Bassey Otu, on Wednesday presented a proposed ₦987.8 billion budget for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly, christening it the “Budget of Consolidation and Renewed Hope”, reaffirming his administration’s commitment to sustainable development, fiscal discipline and inclusive economic growth. Presenting the estimates in Calabar, Otu described the budget as more than an aggregation of figures, characterising it as “a solemn and sacred pact laden with the trust, expectation and aspiration of the people for their improved livelihoods.” He said its successful implementation would depend on prudent resource management, accountability and disciplined public expenditure, underscoring his administration’s determination to translate its social contract with the people into tangible improvements in their living conditions. The proposed budget, valued at precisely ₦987,808,089,235.92, represents an increase of approximately 2.57 per cent over the 2026 budget. Capital expenditure accounts for ₦708.43 billion, representing 71.72 per cent of the total provision, while recurrent expenditure stands at ₦279.38 billion, or 28.28 per cent. The substantial capital allocation, according to the governor, reflects the government’s determination to prioritise infrastructure, human capital development and productive investments capable of stimulating economic activity. Otu explained that the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework and Fiscal Strategy Paper provided the foundation for the estimates, adding that the budget would sustain ongoing programmes while opening new pathways for investment, employment creation and improved public services. “The imperative of this exercise underscores our collective resolve to chart a sustainable course for the growth and development of our dear State,” he declared. Addressing concerns surrounding the state’s debt profile, the governor maintained that his administration had refrained from obtaining fresh domestic and external loans since assuming office in 2023. Citing verifiable indices from the National Bureau of Statistics and the Debt Management Office, he said Cross River remained among the few states that had not contracted new loans during the period. He attributed the state’s existing debt burden to obligations inherited from previous administrations, explaining that debt servicing had constrained the pace at which available resources could be deployed to development projects. He further clarified that the naira value of external debt had been affected by currency devaluation and foreign-exchange liberalisation. “I cannot, and will never mortgage the future of our children with unsustainable loans,” Otu declared, pledging to strengthen internally generated revenue, maximise federal allocations and attract development assistance and private-sector investment to finance the state’s development priorities. Reviewing the performance of the 2026 budget, the governor acknowledged the pressures of exchange-rate volatility, rising operational costs, supply-chain disruptions and inherited debt obligations. He disclosed that the administration had collaborated with the legislature to enact a supplementary budget, raising the spending framework to ₦963.07 billion to accommodate urgent interventions and counterpart-funding requirements. Among the achievements highlighted was the delivery of more than 608 kilometres of interconnected road projects across the three senatorial districts, including the Nsan–Oban Road in Akamkpa, the Adiabo–Ikoneto Road in Odukpani and the Yahe–Ebo–Wanakade Road in Yala. He also reported progress in rural electrification through solar streetlights, mini-grids and network rehabilitation, describing the interventions as essential to reopening economic corridors, improving mobility and restoring commercial activity in underserved communities. Agriculture featured prominently in the governor’s account of the administration’s economic transformation agenda. Otu disclosed that more than 20,000 bags of fertiliser had been distributed to 8,000 farmers, while over one million improved oil-palm, cowpea and cocoa seedlings had been provided to farmers across the state. He also highlighted the establishment of a 50,000-hectare rice project and support for more than 5,300 livestock farmers, alongside loans, grants and agricultural machinery for smallholder and large-scale producers. According to him, an ₦18 billion offtake arrangement had helped advance the state’s agricultural initiatives, while the cash-crop revolution was strengthening the productive capacity of farmers. “There is no food security without agriculture,” he asserted, adding that the government intended to become Nigeria’s leading cocoa and oil-palm-producing state through expanded cultivation, mechanisation, agro-allied industries and private-sector partnerships. On healthcare, education and public-sector welfare, Otu outlined interventions designed to improve access, strengthen institutions and enhance service delivery. He cited the renovation and rehabilitation of hospitals, the establishment of medical oxygen plants in Calabar and Ogoja in partnership with UNICEF, and the upgrading of state-owned Schools of Nursing and Midwifery to accreditation standards. He also highlighted a reported 95 per cent routine immunisation coverage, implementation of the Consolidated Medical Salary Structure for medical workers and an increase in the retirement age of health workers from 60 to 65 years. In education, he said the state had deployed more than ₦17 billion in Universal Basic Education Commission intervention funds, supported classroom construction and rehabilitation, paid WAEC examination fees for 43,694 Cross River State indigenes and approved the promotion of more than 14,000 teaching and non-teaching staff. The government, he added, was targeting a literacy rate of 98 per cent from the current estimated 80.7 per cent, while strengthening technical and vocational education to equip young people with employable and entrepreneurial skills. The 2027 estimates also assign prominent roles to aviation, transportation, maritime development and tourism in the state’s economic diversification strategy. The governor disclosed the integration of a new Bombardier CRJ regional jet into the state’s aviation assets, bringing the fleet to five aircraft, alongside accelerated construction work at the Obudu International Passenger and Cargo Airport. He further highlighted the acquisition of 730 electric vehicles, comprising inter-city and metropolitan buses, tricycles and motorcycles, to reduce commuting costs and support cleaner transportation. On the maritime front, he said the Bakassi Deep Seaport had secured the Federal Government’s approval and Certificate of Compliance and was awaiting the commencement of construction, with anticipated private investment of approximately $3.5 billion. He also cited the federal government’s formal re-accreditation of Cross River as a littoral state, describing it as a strategic development for the state’s maritime ambitions. “Our overall target in this sector is to transform our aviation business model into a highly profitable and self-sustaining revenue asset for the State,” he said. Infrastructure receives the largest explicitly listed sectoral allocation of ₦246.1 billion, followed by education with ₦99.6 billion, health with ₦85.4 billion, agriculture with ₦28.2 billion and aviation with ₦21.8 billion. Other provisions include ₦20.2 billion for the House of Assembly, ₦19.1 billion for the judiciary, ₦16.6 billion for power and ₦11.3 billion for tourism. The governor said the budget would continue to align with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, ensuring continuity in unfinished projects and directing resources towards the state’s strategic priorities. item.title: Barcelona star admits PSG ‘deserved’ win over Barcelona
item.description: Barcelona star admits PSG ‘deserved’ win over Barcelona Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon said Paris St-Germain “deserved” their 4-2 victory over the Spanish Champions. Désiré Doué put the hosts 1-0 ahead going into half-time but Xavi Espart equalised after 55 minutes. PSG were ahead again through Lucas Hernández on 72 minutes although they were pegged back seven minutes later by Lamine Yamal. Vítiniha and Fabián Ruiz scored in the 81 st and 86 th minutes respectively to ensure the Parisians’ perfect start to the Champions League. Following the game, Anthony Gordon said: “I think it was quite predictable that it was going to be high-scoring and a good spectacle for people to watch. I was hoping we would come out on the right side of that, but unfortunately we didn’t. “They deserved it. They were the better team and had the better moments with real quality. Athletically, they were able to sustain the pressure and intensity for longer than we were. They’ve been the team to beat for two years and tonight they gave a great example as to why. “I think we can take great positives because we played well. It was a competitive spectacle. We’ve still got work to do and that’s a good position to be in. Gordon’s team-mate , Raphinha started a game for the first time in over a month for Barcelona after picking up an injury while on international duty for Brazil. He said: “We knew it could happen; we’re facing the two-time European champions, and playing in front of their fans is very tough. “We wanted to come away with a win or a point – whatever – but it’s no big deal; these things happen when they’re meant to, and in the end we’ve only dropped three points. “They are a very well-drilled side. Despite today’s result, we competed well. Both teams like to play with the ball and we had possession. It was a good test and shows we can compete. The result doesn’t matter, but we played well. “After all, I’ve had less than a week’s training, and this was the plan – to play fewer minutes. I finished the match feeling good and strong, and I’m trying to improve my physical condition further.” Manager Hansi Flick told reporters: “I think it was a fantastic game from both teams but we made too many mistakes, especially in possession. “But I also saw a lot of good things. For me it was a great test for us and you also saw today what errors we have to improve to make things better. “We have to learn from this game. Today, in October, you cannot win titles. You win the Champions League in June.” This was the first time that Barcelona had failed to win this season. Before last night they had played 11, won 11 while scoring 48 goals. They host rivals Real Madrid on Sunday in the first El Clásico of the season.

item.title: LeBron James goes all Midwestern on heckling Knicks fans in Philadelphia debut
item.description: LeBron James made his Philadelphia 76ers debut on Tuesday night at Madison Square Garden against the defending champion New York Knicks . It’s safe to say fans at the most famous arena in the world were feeling themselves after finally capturing that elusive championship. MORE: 3 biggest storylines heading into 2026-27 NBA season Having James in the building just added fuel to their fire. Like every other opposing fanbase has done for the past quarter century, New York supporters let him know their every thought for 2.5 hours. Knicks fan heckle James At one point, with Jalen Brunson shooting free throws, James had enough and offered a pointed retort at a courtside heckler. "You don’t know what the fk you talkin about…I’m not from the west coast…I’m from Ohio baby. Ay…Fk you talkin about" –– New NYC resident LeBron James meets his neighbors https://t.co/0eHhcLK2uz — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) October 21, 2026 As a fellow Midwesterner, it’s easy to say that LeBron is exactly correct. It may be unclear what he was driving at here but those of us from flyover country need to stick together. The incomparable Mike Tirico was on the call for NBC and expertly narrated the heated scene . LMAOOOOOOOO https://t.co/bQaPtfQWnX — Shabazz 💫 (@ShowCaseShabazz) October 21, 2026 “He said hello to somebody over here,” Tirico said. “Spike Lee is over for a look and a chat. I heard a guy yell behind me, saying, ‘Hey, LeBron, just because you have a helicopter and you live in New York doesn’t mean we’re gonna cheer for you!’ LeBron is taking the helicopter rides back and forth from Philadelphia to New York and engaged here in some front-row convo.” James responds to MSG fans Tirico’s partner, Reggie Miller, joined in to suggest getting James all riled up might not prove to be the smartest strategy. “That’s the last thing you wanna do is get LeBron going here in this building,” Miller added. “Here’s the guy in question that’s having words with LeBron. And guess who’s playing peacemaker? Spike Lee! He’s over here playing peacemaker. Boy, I have seen everything.” Oct 20, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) untucks his jersey after defeating the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Sure enough, Philadelphia locked into form and secured an opening night victory to make a statement. James was not the first or even second offensive option but did blend pretty seamlessly into a team with a lot of options. Which is another thing you’d expect someone from the Midwest to do. We’re all about the collective and there’s no place for a me-first glory hog. At the end of the day who cares if it’s by helicopter or horseback as long as they show up for their assigned shift. It’s weird f

item.title: MVP urges MMA fighters to form union over pay
item.description: Michael 'Venom' Page joined KSI's Misfits Boxing promotion earlier this month [Getty Images] Michael 'Venom' Page says MMA fighters need to form a union and "move as one" if they want to secure better pay in the sport. The 39-year-old signed a deal with Misfits Boxing earlier this month after leaving the UFC. Page, better known as MVP, won five of his six bouts in the UFC after debuting in 2024 but was critical of the money its fighters earn , compared with top-level athletes in other sports. After joining Misfits, where Page says he will earn "a lot more" than he did in the UFC, the Briton wants to use his platform to empower fellow fighters. Page points to the Muhammad Ali Act - a 2000 US law designed to protect boxers' rights and combat potential monopolies - as something which he'd like to replicate in MMA. "It's less about speaking out now, it's more about forming a union and coming together. We have to move as one," Page told BBC Sport. "If all fighters said 'we're not gonna do it', then UFC doesn't exist. That's the important thing for fighters to remember. It's not just the machine of UFC, you guys are the nuts and bolts that help the machine move. "A fighters union is what's important - the Muhammad Ali Act is what has allowed boxers to be paid well and the same thing needs to happen in MMA." Fighter pay has been questioned by athletes and the media this year after boxer Conor Benn signed a reported £11m one-fight deal with Zuffa Boxing. Zuffa Boxing is owned by UFC president Dana White, so critics have asked why the 57-year-old isn't paying similar amounts to his MMA fighters under contract. White has repeatedly defended fighter pay in the UFC, referencing the promotion's £5.7bn broadcast deal with Paramount. Last week, after criticism from UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland , White pointed to the American signing a new contract in May. Page says criticism like that of Strickland is "common" in the UFC, but most fighters don't speak out in case of repercussions. "You speak to other athletes and it's a very common thing. Most people are not willing to say anything because it will affect them," said Page. "I feel if I don't say anything, silence is going along with it and you're part of the problem. But I also understand you have your own bills to pay, so I'm not against anyone that doesn't either. "If more people spoke out then they'd have to do something but it's difficult if we're not doing it as a unit, you can get ousted and other things can happen." Page says he is "excited" to box in Misfits, and discussions have taken place about incorporating MMA into the promotion, but his main goal is to create a healthier financial space for the younger generation. "The aim is to get them well paid, well looked after and well treated in the MMA space and bring competition against other shows," said Page. Last week, after criticism from UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland , White pointed to the American signing a new contract in May. Page says criticism like that of Strickland is "common" in the UFC, but most fighters don't speak out in case of repercussions. "You speak to other athletes and it's a very common thing. Most people are not willing to say anything because it will affect them," said Page. "I feel if I don't say anything, silence is going along with it and you're part of the problem. But I also understand you have your own bills to pay, so I'm not against anyone that doesn't either. Page says he is "excited" to box in Misfits, and discussions have taken place about incorporating MMA into the promotion, but his main goal is to create a healthier financial space for the younger generation. "The aim is to get them well paid, well looked after and well treated in the MMA space and bring competition against other shows," said Page. "Which is good for fighters, it means they have alternative spaces to go to and they can negotiate better because of it. "I see people in the UFC still struggling and I don't think there's another sport you can get to the top of your field and be struggling financially. I definitely want better for fighters." I loved UFC for the most part - Page Despite his criticisms of fighter pay, Page says he "for the most part loved" his time in the UFC. He praised the promotion's staff, its Performance Institute - regarded as the gold standard among MMA training facilities - and its fans. However, Page, who won all of his fights in the promotion by decision, faced criticism from fans over his lack of knockouts and admits he might have approached things differently in hindsight. "I wish I could have done more with my performances, but overall I loved it," he said. "I think the game has slightly shifted. It's not about who's the most skilled anymore, it's about guys who are willing to put themselves through hell and shave years off their life every single time they fight. "If I was a bit more aware of that I would have shifted a little bit to try and compensate for that." Page says he's aiming to make his debut in Misfits "in the first part of next year" but it has not been decided if it will be under boxing or MMA rules. He mentioned former UFC stars Nate Diaz and Darren Till as interesting match-ups, but reiterated that no discussions about potential opponents have taken place yet. item.title: UEFA Champions League Preview: Inter vs Shakhtar Donetsk – Team News, Lineups & Preview
item.description: UEFA Champions League Preview: Inter vs Shakhtar Donetsk – Team News, Lineups & Preview Stadio Giuseppe Meazza forms the backdrop for Inter Milan’s first UEFA Champions League clash against Shakhtar Donetsk since November 2021. The Ukrainian giants’ arrival looks like a prime opportunity for the Nerazzurri to bounce back from a stunning 4-3 home defeat to Club Brugge last time out. Cristian Chivu’s side kicked off this season’s league phase with a whimper. After a 2-1 loss at Real Madrid on matchday one, Inter unexpectedly lost to Club Brugge on home turf, suffering back-to-back defeats at the start of a new Champions League campaign for the first time since 2006/07. However, the reigning Serie A champions switfly got back on track in the domestic championship. Despite conceding the opening goal in Saturday’s away encounter against Bologna, they pulled off another comeback to secure a 3-1 win at Renato Dall’Ara and solidify their place at the top of the table. Like their hosts, Shakhtar come into this meeting on the back of another domestic triumph as they beat Kolos Kovalivka 2-1 at home to maintain a two-point lead at the Ukrainian Premier League’s summit. Yet, unlike Inter, Arda Turan’s men have managed to translate their domestic supremacy to the continental scene. Shakhtar held PSV Eindhoven to a commendable 1-1 draw on matchday one before putting AEK Athens to the sword last week. Goals on either side of halftime propelled the 16-time Ukrainian champions to a convincing 3-1 victory, marking their best two-game Champions League start since 2014/15. Match Preview Inter Not only have Inter started a new Champions League season with consecutive losses for the first time in two decades, but they’re also experiencing their longest losing streak in this competition. Chivu’s men have lost four Champions League games in a row and have been beaten in seven of their last eight outings in Europe’s most prestigious club tournament (W1). Perhaps another match at Meazza could inspire a much-needed resurgence, but the Nerazzurri would be well-advised not to take anything for granted after losing their last four Champions League fixtures here. If it’s any consolation, those four losses remain their only home defeats in any competition since the start of December 2025 (W16, D3). Determined to put a negative club record in Europe to bed, Inter can draw confidence from their imperious run against Shakhtar. A 2-0 home win in their last meeting five years ago upheld their unbeaten record against this opposition (W3, D4) while also marking their sixth clean sheet in seven head-to-heads. Shakhtar Donetsk Without a goal in their last five clashes against Inter, Shkahtar must punch above their weight if they’re to avoid defeat in their opening three matches of a Champions League season for the first time since 2014/15, when they reached the knockout stages.
