item.content:encoded: UEFA Champions League Preview: Inter vs Shakhtar Donetsk – Team News, Lineups & Preview Stadio Giuseppe Meazza forms the backdrop for Inter Milan’s first UEFA Champions League clash against Shakhtar Donetsk since November 2021. The Ukrainian giants’ arrival looks like a prime opportunity for the Nerazzurri to bounce back from a stunning 4-3 home defeat to Club Brugge last time out. Cristian Chivu’s side kicked off this season’s league phase with a whimper. After a 2-1 loss at Real Madrid on matchday one, Inter unexpectedly lost to Club Brugge on home turf, suffering back-to-back defeats at the start of a new Champions League campaign for the first time since 2006/07. However, the reigning Serie A champions switfly got back on track in the domestic championship. Despite conceding the opening goal in Saturday’s away encounter against Bologna, they pulled off another comeback to secure a 3-1 win at Renato Dall’Ara and solidify their place at the top of the table. Like their hosts, Shakhtar come into this meeting on the back of another domestic triumph as they beat Kolos Kovalivka 2-1 at home to maintain a two-point lead at the Ukrainian Premier League’s summit. Yet, unlike Inter, Arda Turan’s men have managed to translate their domestic supremacy to the continental scene. Shakhtar held PSV Eindhoven to a commendable 1-1 draw on matchday one before putting AEK Athens to the sword last week. Goals on either side of halftime propelled the 16-time Ukrainian champions to a convincing 3-1 victory, marking their best two-game Champions League start since 2014/15. Match Preview Inter Not only have Inter started a new Champions League season with consecutive losses for the first time in two decades, but they’re also experiencing their longest losing streak in this competition. Chivu’s men have lost four Champions League games in a row and have been beaten in seven of their last eight outings in Europe’s most prestigious club tournament (W1). Perhaps another match at Meazza could inspire a much-needed resurgence, but the Nerazzurri would be well-advised not to take anything for granted after losing their last four Champions League fixtures here. If it’s any consolation, those four losses remain their only home defeats in any competition since the start of December 2025 (W16, D3). Determined to put a negative club record in Europe to bed, Inter can draw confidence from their imperious run against Shakhtar. A 2-0 home win in their last meeting five years ago upheld their unbeaten record against this opposition (W3, D4) while also marking their sixth clean sheet in seven head-to-heads. Shakhtar Donetsk Without a goal in their last five clashes against Inter, Shkahtar must punch above their weight if they’re to avoid defeat in their opening three matches of a Champions League season for the first time since 2014/15, when they reached the knockout stages. However, history sides with Inter here. Ukrainian clubs have drawn a blank in their last nine matches against Italian teams (D4, L5) since Shakhtar’s win over Atalanta in 2019, perhaps best illustrating the size of the task awaiting Turan’s side on Wednesday. By contrast, the visitors head into proceedings amid a purple patch, having won ten of their 12 competitive fixtures this season (D1, L1), including the last seven on the trot. Shakhtar’s red-hot form offers the traveling fans some hope, as they’ve grown tired of seeing their side flop on the road. Indeed, they’ve gone winless in their last seven away games in the Champions League proper (D2, L5) despite finding the back of the net on five occasions in that dreadful sequence. Team News In addition to long-term absentee John Stones, Inter will also be without Benjamin Pavard and Curtis Jones, who are recovering from thigh injuries. Furthermore, Lautaro Martinez will be on the sidelines until the next international break, meaning either Ange-Yoan Bonny or Francesco Pio Esposito will partner up with free-firing Marcus Thuram in attack. Meanwhile, Shakhtar will arrive in Italy without Eguinaldo and Alaa Ghram, with Marlon Santos and Diego Arroyo unlikely to feature due to lingering fitness problems. Nevertheless, star forwards Pedrinho and Kaua Elias are expected to start despite not being allowed to rest at the weekend. Inter vs Shakhtar Donetsk Potential Starting Lineups Inter (3-5-2): J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Bastoni; Diouf, Barella, Calhanoglu, Mkhitaryan, Dimarco; Thuram, Esposito. Shakhtar Donetsk (4-2-3-1): Riznyk; Tobias, Bondar, Matviyenko, P. Henrique; Ocheretko, Gomes; Santana, Pedrinho, Newerton; Elias. Inter vs Shakhtar Donetsk Prediction There is no margin for error here if Inter are to return in contention for a place in the knockout stages. Despite Shakhtar’s scintillating form and a promising Champions League start, this is Inter’s match to lose, and we can’t see the Nerazzurri dropping more points on home turf.

item.title: Jury selection set for trial of driver in Gaudreau crash
item.description: Jury selection is to begin Dec. 1 for the motorist who fatally struck hockey star Johnny Gaudreau and his brother as they bicycled on a rural road in South Jersey in August 2024. Superior Court Judge Michael Silvanio has set the process to begin at 9 a.m. in his courtroom at the Salem County Courthouse. Trial is scheduled to begin Jan. 4 for the driver, 45-year-old Sean Higgins of Pilesgrove. Court fight: Judge in Gaudreau brothers' case won't dismiss indictment Authorities say Higgins struck Johnny Gaudreau, 31, and Matty Gaudreau, 29, as the brothers bicycled on Aug. 29 at approximately 8:20 p.m. on a narrow road in Salem County. Separately, previously unreleased photographs from the accident scene have been made public as part of an Oct. 5 filing by Higgins' defense attorneys. The photos include images of two bicycles shattered by the accident and of Higgins' damaged Jeep. Among other points, the defense filing disputes the prosecution's account of how the accident occurred. It describes as "impossible" the prosecution's assertion that Higgins was passing a vehicle on the right, with his Jeep half on the road's shoulder and half on grass, when he struck the brothers at high speed. Higgins' attorneys — Richard Klineburger III and Matthew Portello, both of Haddonfield — also dispute the prosecution's claim that the driver was drunk at the time of the accident. The Gaudreaus, both of whom were expectant fathers, died at the scene. Johnny Gaudreau was an all-star for the NHL's Columbus Blue Jackets. Known as "Johnny Hockey," he and his brother were South Jersey natives and graduates of Gloucester Catholic High School in Gloucester City. An indictment accuses Higgins of two counts of reckless vehicular homicide while driving drunk. He also faces charges of aggravated manslaughter, evidence tampering and leaving the scene of a fatal accident. The charges are only allegations. Higgins has not been convicted in the case. He has been held in Salem County Jail since the crash. Jim Walsh is a senior reporter with the Courier-Post, Burlington County Times and The Daily Journal. Email: Jwalsh@cpsj.com. Superior Court Judge Michael Silvanio has set the process to begin at 9 a.m. in his courtroom at the Salem County Courthouse. Trial is scheduled to begin Jan. 4 for the driver, 45-year-old Sean Higgins of Pilesgrove. Court fight: Judge in Gaudreau brothers' case won't dismiss indictment Authorities say Higgins struck Johnny Gaudreau, 31, and Matty Gaudreau, 29, as the brothers bicycled on Aug. 29 at approximately 8:20 p.m. on a narrow road in Salem County. Separately, previously unreleased photographs from the accident scene have been made public as part of an Oct. 5 filing by Higgins' defense attorneys. The photos include images of two bicycles shattered by the accident and of Higgins' damaged Jeep. Among other points, the defense filing disputes the prosecution's account of how the accident occurred. item.title: NBA opening day winners and losers: LeBron James and Jaylen Brown solid in debuts, Jayson Tatum struggles
item.description: NBA opening day winners and losers: LeBron James and Jaylen Brown solid in debuts, Jayson Tatum struggles originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NBA experimented with a new scheduling format, and the NBA's season opener was an all-day affair that started at 3 p.m. ET. The Celtics at Pistons , Sixers at Knicks , and Thunder at Spurs were all entertaining affairs that began to shed some light on some of the biggest questions of the year. How would the Celtics fare after the loss of Jaylen Brown? Were people failing to give the Pistons enough credit after recording the best record in the East last year? How would LeBron James and Jaylen Brown fit on the Sixers? Who is the best team in the West? We don't know the answers yet, but we have a better idea after Tuesday's games. MORE: SN experts predictions | Power Rankings NBA opening day winners and losers Winner: Paul George The Celtics had a disastrous opener, blowing a 22-point lead in the third quarter and fumbling away the game in a 121-113 loss. George was the biggest bright spot though. He looked amazing in helping to build that lead up. Boston was the perfect fit for George on paper, and he proved it in practice. Midway through the third quarter, he had already broken the franchise record for points in a debut with 31. He finished with a game-high 38, drilling 3's, getting to the line, and finishing at the rim. George was excellent defensively as well, recording four steals in the first half and five for the game. Even if he plays half as well as he did in his debut, the Jaylen Brown trade will end up as a win for Boston. Loser: Jayson Tatum Tatum, on the other hand, was mostly awful. The expectation was that he could fill into Brown's role from last year. He did playmake for others, recording 11 assists on the day. His shot selection was mostly terrible though, and he was an ugly 6-of-23 from the field. Brutal https://t.co/hn7wY294c8 — KlawWrld (@kawhi_ring) October 21, 2026 Tatum missed all seven of his 3-pointers. More concerning was how ineffective he was at the rim. That marks a continuation from last season, where his rim attempts and percentages were down from his career marks. It's obviously only one game, but Tatum's effectiveness at the rim post-Achilles surgery and Boston's ability in general to generate paint touches are both worth keeping an eye on as the season progresses. Loser: Pistons offense in the first half The Pistons looked rough in scoring only 45 points in the first half. Their poor spacing from last year looked unresolved. The Celtics were essentially ignoring Ausar Thompson any time he was on the perimeter. Detroit badly needed some shooting to emerge. That happened after halftime, where they completely flipped what was looking like a blowout loss into a gritty win. The Celtics were essentially ignoring Ausar Thompson any time he was on the perimeter. Detroit badly needed some shooting to emerge. That happened after halftime, where they completely flipped what was looking like a blowout loss into a gritty win. Winner: Pistons offense in the second half Back when Javonte Green played for the Bulls , the great late announcer Stacey King would proudly proclaim that there were five Javontes on the floor. Green brought that same Chicago energy in his 18 minutes. And more importantly, he hit 5-of-8 from deep, swinging the game. The Pistons outscored the Celtics by an astounding 21 points while he was on the floor. Duncan Robinson got in on the fun later, chipping in five threes as well. That shooting flurry helped the Pistons go on a ridiculous 23-0 run in the second half, sealing an embarrassing loss for the Celtics and showing what they thought of prognosticators like myself putting them outside the top four of the East. MORE: Win projections for every team in the Eastern Conference Winner: LeBron James and Jaylen Brown The Sixers need LeBron to fill a new role, where he will primarily be a facilitator. He had a well-balanced 14 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists in his 34 minutes of play, leading the Sixers to a 106-100 win over the defending champion Knicks. King James did exactly what was asked of him, throwing darts to teammates, getting out in transition for some easy baskets, and finishing on his downhill drives. He looked more comfortable in the second half as he found a rhythm. Brown had a good all-around game as well, scoring 19 points to go along with eight rebounds and six assists. He had some good chemistry with LeBron, getting his first basket off a LeBron assist and setting LeBron up for a fun alley-oop. PSA: Jaylen Brown and LeBron James are Sixers https://t.co/jLy2Mq5Ahc — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) October 21, 2026 MORE: What we learned about LeBron James, new-look 76ers in win over Knicks Loser: Sixers' center rotation Embiid shot just 4-of-15 for the night, settling mostly for jumpers that lacked touch. The rough shooting night was counteracted by relatively good defense. That was spurred by a change at halftime where he asked to switch off Karl-Anthony Towns in favor of an easier assignment in Josh Hart. There were certainly some moments where Embiid looked slow . There were others though, such as his two blocks on Andre Drummond in the second half, where he was moving better than he had in years. Knicks are 12-31 in the paint with Joel on the floor tonight. Had a couple of big blocks on Drummond. — Nate Duncan (@NateDuncanNBA) October 21, 2026 Embiid's backups were not as effective. Adem Bona logged 10 minutes, and Jabari Walker lasted for less than three before Nick Nurse pulled the plug. Both looked like liabilities, particularly against the size of Drummond. We all suspected the Sixers' big man depth was going to be an issue, and that looks very true after the opener. They were able to overcome it on Tuesday, but that problem isn't going away until some sort of roster change happens. Brad Penner-Imagn Images Loser: Karl-Anthony Towns Towns came alive late, scoring 10 of his 19 points in the fourth quarter. But his penchant for committing silly fouls came back, and he was limited to only 23 minutes in a game where Jalen Brunson's shot wasn't falling. Winner: Andre Drummond There was some deep worry about how Drummond would fare as the primary backup behind Towns given how much Drummond fell off the last two seasons with the Sixers. Instead of being a weak point, Drummond looked like the best player on the floor during the first half. He was everywhere, leading the team in minutes and securing a 10-point, 12-rebound double-double by halftime. Drummond slowed down considerably in the second half, going just 1-of-5 and missing wildly on some easy bunnies. That's been the Drummond experience, but the Knicks will happily take this overall performance every night. Winner: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander Most media members have Victor Wembanyama as the favorite for MVP over the reigning two-time winner in SGA. That might be a bit premature. Gilgeous-Alexander showed why he was the best player in the world in the Thunder's dominant 116-104 win over the Spurs. He was draining tough shot after tough shot, getting to the midrange at will and finding pockets where he could avoid Wemby's long arms. The defense was there too. SGA had a Wemby-esque three steals and three impressive blocks for the game, and the Thunder's defense was suffocating as a whole. Winner: Thunder depth, Aday Mara There was some concern Oklahoma City would take a step back after losing Lu Dort, replacing him in the starting lineup with Cason Wallace, and also trading away Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins off the bench. Instead of having depth concerns, the Thunder looked like they had too many guys to play. Mark Daigneault went 11 players deep before garbage time hit. Wallace understood the assignment, introducing himself in the starting lineup as coming from "Clamps University" and playing solid defense on the night. Jared McCain hit seemingly every shot he took, scoring 20 off the bench. Aday Mara's play deserved special attention. item.title: Sturgis 200 medley relay team clocks state-qualifying time
item.description: The Sturgis swim team has continued to improve in the pool this season. The Trojans are not a big team by numbers, but solid performances throughout the season have helped them continue to gain confidence. The Trojans traveled north to take on Mason, Otsego and Wayland in prep swimming action last Saturday, Oct. 17. The highlight for the Trojans was the 200 medley relay team, which qualified for the state finals this year in a time of 1:58.09. The team of Brooklyn Draper, Lilly Whitehead, Ainsley Gump and Katelyn Halling brought home first place in that race. For the meet, Sturgis racked up 554 points in the pool, beating Mason's 524, Wayland's 498 and Otsego's 196. Gump swam to first place in the 200 freestyle at 2:02.21 and was first in the 100 freestyle race at 55.96 seconds. REST OF THE WEEK: Here's a look at the prep sports schedule for the week October 19-24 WEEK 9 FOTBALL PRIMER: Week 9 football primer | Sturgis, Three Rivers renew rivalry in finale The Lady Trojans have now claimed victory in four meets this season, including three in the conference to date. Sturgis also claimed first place in the 200 freestyle relay. There, the team of Gump, Ella Whitehead, Lilly Whitehead and Halling posted 1:47.01 to win. The Trojans were upended 119-63 last week against the Harper Creek Beavers. Herblet won the 200 freestyle at 2:15.53, and Gump won the 200 individual medley at 2:19.77. Gump also swam to first place in the 100 fly with a time of 1:06.97. The Trojans got a victory from the 200 freestyle relay as well with Gump, Whitehead, Whitehead and Halling recording a time of 1:49.05 to pace the field. Sturgis did beat rival Marshall in the pool recently as well, 93-72. That matchup saw Gump finish with a time of 2:13.63, which set a new pool record at Marshall. She won the race. Gump also took first place in the 100 fly on the day with a time of 1:12.73. The 200 medley team picked up a victory in Marshall at 2:01.00 with Gump, Draper, Lilly Whitehead and Halling. They set a MISCA cut time with that race. Also registering wins in Marshall were Herblet in the 200 freestyle at 2:19.49; Halling in the sprint freestyles (27.44 seconds in the 50 and 1:03.42 in the 100); Draper in the 100 backstroke (1:11.22) and the 200 freestyle relay team of Whitehead, Whitehead, Halling and Gump at 1:50.03. Contact Sports Editor Brandon Watson at bwatson@gannett.com . Follow him on X, formerly known as Twitter, @BwatsonSJ. This article originally appeared on Sturgis Journal: Sturgis 200 medley relay team clocks state-qualifying time

item.title: Hoffenheim vs. Lyon preview: Team news & predicted lineups
item.description: Hoffenheim vs. Lyon preview: Team news & predicted lineups After a much-needed 2-1 win over fellow Bundesliga strugglers Borussia Mönchengladbach ended their four-game losing streak at the weekend, TSG Hoffenheim will be looking to build on that result when they face Olympique Lyon in the Europa League on Thursday. Die Kraichgauer desperately need points in the Europa League, having lost 2-0 to both OFI and Besiktas in their first two games in the competition this season. By contrast, Lyon have won both of their Europa League encounters so far, beating Anderlecht 2-1 away from home before edging Crystal Palace 3-2 on home soil. Paulo Fonseca's side have also impressed domestically, maintaining top spot on goal difference ahead of Paris Saint-Germain with a 2-1 win over OGC Nice at the weekend. The two teams also met in the Europa League in 2024, playing out a 2-2 draw in a game that saw Umut Tohumcu rescue a point for Hoffenheim with a late equaliser in injury time. Team news and predicted lineups: TSG Hoffenheim will have to manage without Nathan de Cat, Albian Hajdari and Patrick Wimmer, who are all injured. Head coach Christian Ilzer could rotate his side, as he has done in Europe earlier this season, with Kicker speculating that Valentin Gendrey could be handed his first start of the campaign at right-back at the expense of veteran Vladimir Coufal. Further forward, veteran striker Andrej Kramarić is among those likely to come into the starting lineup, having played a more marginal role this season and been limited to just 12 minutes against Gladbach at the weekend. As for Lyon, Paulo Fonseca is also likely to make some changes to his side, having similarly rotated his squad in Europe this season. Loïs Openda, Mohamadi Ouedraogo and Nicolás Tagliafico are set to miss out through injury for the visitors. Click here to see our predicted Hoffenheim vs. Lyon lineups.

item.title: Week 7 Fantasy Football Mailbag: Is Germie Bernard or Omar Cooper Jr. Better for the Rest of the Season?
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard (17) scores a /td/ during overtime against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Rookie wideouts have been the craze on the fantasy football waiver wire in recent weeks, with Germie Bernard and Omar Cooper Jr. emerging as enticing options for WR-needy teams. Bernard and Cooper are both viable additions, but if you're stuck between them, it's worth discussing their rest-of-season outlooks. In this week's installment of our fantasy football mailbag, which questions are eating away at managers? Note: Feel free to reach out to me on Twitter so I can answer your fantasy football questions in future articles. All stats used in this article are from PFF or Sumer Sports unless stated otherwise. Fantasy rankings and fantasy point totals are courtesy of FantasyPros . Should Managers Target Germie Bernard or Omar Cooper Jr. as the Better Option for the Rest of the Season? Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard (17) carries the ball in the second half against the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Bernard appeared in my Week 6 FAAB report as my favorite player to target on the waiver wire. The first-year WR on the Pittsburgh Steelers responded by finishing Week 6 as the WR3 in fantasy points (25.7) with 11 receptions, 87 yards, and a touchdown. With Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson both on injured reserve for the Steelers, Bernard is primed to become a go-to target for Aaron Rodgers the rest of the season. DK Metcalf has also been extremely inefficient in 2026, making it a non-zero chance that Bernard is already the No. 1 WR in Pittsburgh. As for Cooper, the first-round pick by the New York Jets produced a season-high 22.3 fantasy points to conclude Week 6 as the WR6. Even with Garrett Wilson operating as the Jets' featured wideout, Cooper led the team in targets (7), receptions (6), and receiving yards (103) on Sunday against the New England Patriots. Although it's an extremely small sample, Cooper has the seventh-most yards after the catch per reception (7.3) and most yards per route run (4.59) among WRs with five-plus targets. Between Bernard and Cooper, Bernard would be my preferred choice for the rest of the season. Cooper has to compete for targets with Wilson, and it remains to be seen what his role looks like once Adonai Mitchell returns and if rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq gets more involved. item.title: Week 7 fantasy football RB start-sit: Dowdle, Mason, Pollard, Wilson
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers running back Rico Dowdle is a Week 7 fantasy football start ’em pick against the Saints in Paris, and Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard is a sit ’em pick against the Browns. item.title: Essex sign wicketkeeper Bell from Lancashire
item.description: George Bell spent the end of the 2026 season on loan at Essex [Getty Images] Essex have signed wicketkeeper George Bell from Lancashire on a permanent two-year deal after a productive loan spell last season. The 24-year-old made three Essex appearances at the end of the 2026 campaign, scoring a half-century in each innings and finishing in the 60s on every occasion. "I believe this is an environment that will help me to develop my game further and hopefully contribute to Essex wins and trophies," Bell told the club's website. Bell made his first-class debut for Lancashire in 2022, and has represented England at under-21 level. Across 37 first-class matches, he has scored more than 1,400 runs, including nine half-centuries, with a high score of 99. Essex's director of cricket, Chris Silverwood, said: "Not only were George's performances impressive on the field, but the way he carried himself, his attitude, work ethic and mindset also impressed us. "We felt George had more than earned the opportunity to join us on a permanent deal, and we are delighted to now have him. He has already shown what he can bring to the team, and we are all excited about his addition to the squad."

item.title: The Rams worked out 42-year old Matt Prater
item.description: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 25: Matt Prater #5 and Markus Golden #44 of the Arizona Cardinals interact with Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams after their game at State Farm Stadium on September 25, 2022 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Mike Christy/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matt Prater is one of the best NFL kickers viewers have had the privilege to watch for years. He maybe almost joined the Los Angeles Rams. Now, Prater has been in the league since 2006 so with that longevity comes experience, but age. Age equating to diminished performance can be the end of an NFL career. Prater specialized as a long-distance kicker with the most 50+ yard field goals made in NFL history . Prime Prater with Sean McVay would’ve been a cheat code for points. McVay did somewhat have this type of kicker with Greg Zuerlein , he was great when he was great, but Prater was a bit better. All that aside, the Rams are going with Brandon McManus. You could say I buried the lede down here , but how desperate are the Rams for a kicker? Very desperate. As their dream turned nightmare season rolls along. Brandon McManus is latest signing in Rams’ kicker carousel (clutchpoints) “The Los Angeles Rams are signing veteran kicker Brandon McManus , their third kicker of the 2026 NFL season. The move follows Blake Grupe’s torn ACL during Sunday’s 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium. McManus, 35, worked out Tuesday alongside free-agent kicker Matt Prater as Los Angeles addressed its special-teams problems. The Rams are 2-4 after six games and hope the veteran can bring stability to the position. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport shared details of the agreement Tuesday on X, formerly Twitter, citing information gathered alongside fellow insider Mike Garafolo.“ NFC West standings: Rams fall to last place, 4 games behind 49ers (ramswire) “It doesn’t help that the Rams have already lost to the 49ers, too, so they can’t sweep San Francisco and clinch that tiebreaker in the event that they finish with the same record. They’ll have to finish with a better divisional record than the 49ers in that case, which seems unlikely considering San Francisco is 3-0 and the Rams are 0-2. The Rams have to go on a run before their Week 11 bye. They’ve got four winnable games coming up, one of which is a rematch against the Cardinals in Week 10. Their other opponents are the Raiders , Chargers and Commanders, who are all at or below .500.“ Past NFC Champ Takes Swipe at Rams for Losing to Mike LaFleur, Cardinals (heavy.com) “Cardinals veteran wide receiver Kendrick Bourne blasted LA via Instagram in a post that surfaced after the 18-16 victory. He believes the Rams haven’t looked efficient on offense without LaFleur there. “Them boys ain’t the same wit out LaFleur,” Bourne posted on his personal IG page. item.content:encoded: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 25: Matt Prater #5 and Markus Golden #44 of the Arizona Cardinals interact with Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams after their game at State Farm Stadium on September 25, 2022 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Mike Christy/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matt Prater is one of the best NFL kickers viewers have had the privilege to watch for years. He maybe almost joined the Los Angeles Rams. Now, Prater has been in the league since 2006 so with that longevity comes experience, but age. Age equating to diminished performance can be the end of an NFL career. Prater specialized as a long-distance kicker with the most 50+ yard field goals made in NFL history . Prime Prater with Sean McVay would’ve been a cheat code for points. McVay did somewhat have this type of kicker with Greg Zuerlein , he was great when he was great, but Prater was a bit better. All that aside, the Rams are going with Brandon McManus. You could say I buried the lede down here , but how desperate are the Rams for a kicker? Very desperate. As their dream turned nightmare season rolls along. Brandon McManus is latest signing in Rams’ kicker carousel (clutchpoints) “The Los Angeles Rams are signing veteran kicker Brandon McManus , their third kicker of the 2026 NFL season. The move follows Blake Grupe’s torn ACL during Sunday’s 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium. McManus, 35, worked out Tuesday alongside free-agent kicker Matt Prater as Los Angeles addressed its special-teams problems. The Rams are 2-4 after six games and hope the veteran can bring stability to the position. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport shared details of the agreement Tuesday on X, formerly Twitter, citing information gathered alongside fellow insider Mike Garafolo.“ NFC West standings: Rams fall to last place, 4 games behind 49ers (ramswire) “It doesn’t help that the Rams have already lost to the 49ers, too, so they can’t sweep San Francisco and clinch that tiebreaker in the event that they finish with the same record. They’ll have to finish with a better divisional record than the 49ers in that case, which seems unlikely considering San Francisco is 3-0 and the Rams are 0-2. The Rams have to go on a run before their Week 11 bye. They’ve got four winnable games coming up, one of which is a rematch against the Cardinals in Week 10. Their other opponents are the Raiders , Chargers and Commanders, who are all at or below .500.“ Past NFC Champ Takes Swipe at Rams for Losing to Mike LaFleur, Cardinals (heavy.com) “Cardinals veteran wide receiver Kendrick Bourne blasted LA via Instagram in a post that surfaced after the 18-16 victory. He believes the Rams haven’t looked efficient on offense without LaFleur there. “Them boys ain’t the same wit out LaFleur,” Bourne posted on his personal IG page. LaFleur worked under McVay as offensive coordinator before accepting the Cardinals head coaching opening in the 2026 offseason. He became the latest past McVay OC to land a head coaching gig; following the path of brother Matt LaFleur, Zac Taylor, and Kevin O’Connell. The latter three have guided playoff runs or, in the case of the Cincinnati Bengals head coach Taylor, a Super Bowl appearance against the Rams in 2021.“ Rams put 2 players on IR, officially sign new kicker (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams made a trio of roster moves on Tuesday, all of which were expected. They placed Davante Adams and Poona Ford on injured reserve and signed kicker Brandon McManus to replace Blake Grupe. Interestingly, they did not put Kobie Turner on IR yet, though Sean McVay said on Monday that the team will likely move him there at some point; he’s expected to miss a “handful of weeks,” as McVay put it. Adams will be out 6-10 weeks with a ruptured hamstring, while Ford will miss the rest of the season with a torn triceps. Turner injured his groin in Sunday’s loss but McVay didn’t have an exact timetable for his return.“ Rams are gambling on Brandon McManus being past his Packers collapse (ramblinfan) “Last season, McManus ranked 43rd out 43 kickers as measured by FanSided’s Kick Value Added metric. he names directly above him? Ironically enough, LA’s Joshua Karty and Grupe. Hopefully McManus can keep those gargoyles at bay for as long as the Rams must rely on him. Brandon McManus isn’t dependable, but he’ll have to do for the Rams McManus did, at least, beat out an ancient Matt Prater in Tuesday’s audition. If you’re looking for more robust reassurance, well, there really isn’t any, but McManus was highly effective in 2024, his first Packers season.“ NFL Power Rankings Week 7: Rams Fall 12 Spots, Steelers Up 5 (nfl.com) “Check out Nick Shook’s Power Rankings for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL Season.” 49ers fans can laugh at the Rams (but it would be foolish to count them out) (ninernoise) “While it is more than fair, and probably even encouraged, to laugh at the Rams right now, it would be silly to count them out entirely. Yes, they have been really bad and have had some key injuries, but they still have a lot of talent on the roster, and it would be surprising if head coach Sean McVay isn’t able to figure something out by the end of the season. The Myles Garrett trade has not worked out as planned, and Davante Adams is going to be out for a while. But the Rams’ upcoming schedule is not especially scary, and if they get some of their guys back late in the season and start to peak for the playoffs, then they will definitely be a team no one wants to face in the playoffs.“ Jaguars could gift LA Rams a WR spark with Brian Thomas Jr. trade (blackandteal) “The Washington Commanders most definitely make sense because of Thomas’ LSU connection with quarterback Jayden Daniels . However, there’s another club in the NFC that would make a push for him. The Jaguars could trade Brian Thomas Jr. to the LA Rams in return for a 2nd-round pick Like other teams that are dealing with injuries at receiver, Los Angeles would be a realistic landing spot for Brian Thomas Jr. While Puka Nacua is back in the fold after sitting out two contests with a groin and a core muscle injury, teammate Davante Adams will tentatively miss six to 10 games after sustaining a hamstring rupture . Brian Thomas Jr. would be a more than capable replacement, as Michel Haney at Ramblin Fan suggests. Here’s the skinny.“ 5 things to know about new Rams kicker Brandon McManus (ramswire) “Here are five things to know about the Rams’ new kicker. He’s a Super Bowl champion Before the Broncos went on a decade-long playoff drought that lasted after McManus’ departure, he won Super Bowl 50 with the team. During that playoff run, McManus hit all 10 field goal attempts and was perfect in point-after attempts.“ Raiders Won’t Face Former Star Davante Adams as Rams Lose Key Players (sports.yahoo) “Adams, 33, spent parts of three seasons with the Raiders after arriving in a blockbuster trade with the Green Bay Packers in 2022. He was traded to the New York Jets during the 2024 season before joining the Rams. Sunday’s game would have marked his first appearance against the Raiders since leaving Las Vegas. Adams had been one of the Rams’ most productive offensive players this season, catching 30 passes for 480 yards and four touchdowns through six games. His absence is another significant setback for Los Angeles, which has struggled to a 2-4 start.“ Comment of the Day: “McManus is an experienced kicker in the NFL unlike Tanner whose glory came in the UFL. Rams obviously looking for someone with experience based off of who they brought in. I’ll go with the Rams in this one.” -TonyT828 Feed post of the day:

item.title: Barcelona confirm Dani Olmo injury ahead of El Clasico test
item.description: PARIS, FRANCE - OCTOBER 20: Dani Olmo #20 of Barcelona during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 football match between Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and FC Barcelona at Parc des Princes stadium on October 20, 2026 in Paris, France. (Photo by Jean Catuffe/Getty Images) | Getty Images Barcelona have confirmed that Dani Olmo will miss around a month of action after sustaining an injury in Tuesday’s Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain. Olmo had to be replaced in the first half at the Parc des Princes and is now set for a spell on the sidelines. “Tests carried out confirm that Dani Olmo is suffering from an injury to his left adductor muscle as a consequence of a collision with an opponent during the game against Paris Saint-Germain,” read a club statement. “The player is expected to be out for around a month.” Olmo joins Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen in the treatment room at Barcelona. Jules Kounde is also sidelined but it’s hoped he could be passed fit for Sunday’s El Clasico against Real Madrid. As for Olmo, he’ll also miss games against Alaves, Atletico Madrid and Villarreal in La Liga as well as the Champions League fixtures with Aston Villa and Sabah.

item.title: Courtois talks Mbappe, Lamine Yamal, Vinicius, Ballon d’Or, renewal: ‘Individually no one has been better than him’
item.description: Courtois talks Mbappe, Lamine Yamal, Vinicius, Ballon d’Or, renewal: ‘Individually no one has been better than him’ Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois believes his teammate Kylian Mbappe deserves to win the Ballon d’Or, insisting that nobody has been better than the Frenchman ‘individually’, while questioning the criteria used to determine the award. The Belgian goalkeeper believes his Real Madrid teammate deserves recognition for his individual performances, although he acknowledged that Lamine Yamal has the advantage of having won major trophies with Barcelona and Spain. Courtois throws his weight behind Mbappe “I think Kylian deserves it, but people vote according to their own logic,” Courtois told DAZN (h/t AS ), just days before the Ballon d’Or ceremony, which will take place in London next Monday. Courtois highlighted the dilemma between rewarding individual performances and collective succes, saying: “Do we choose someone who has won trophies, or someone who has been above everyone else throughout the season, even if they have not won anything? “I am thinking especially of Kylian. I think individually nobody has been better than Kylian, but unfortunately, we have not won anything collectively.” One of the contenders for Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The Belgian recalled that Mbappe finished fourth at the World Cup and was the tournament’s top scorer, while his main rival for the award, Lamine Yamal, became world champion with Spain. “For me, Lamine Yamal had a slightly worse World Cup, but he became world champion, won La Liga with Barcelona and had a good year,” said the 34-year-old goalkeeper. Courtois also questioned the voting criteria, recalling that he expected Vinicius Jr. or Dani Carvajal to win the 2024 award, only for Spain midfielder Rodri to take the prize. “I did not think it had been his best year, although he won the European Championship with Spain. The previous year, when City won the Champions League, I think he would have deserved to win it,” Courtois said. He added that “sometimes it is difficult to know how to vote for the Ballon d’Or”. Contract renewal at Real Madrid Turning to his future at Real Madrid, Courtois said he expects to finalise a contract extension soon. His current deal expires in June 2027, with an agreement for another year understood to be close . “It is not finalised yet. In principle, it should be resolved quickly. There is no problem. We simply need to find time for my agent and my father to discuss the final details,” he explained. “I want to stay here for a long time, and I am doing everything I can to make that happen,” he added. Courtois will sign a new contract until 2028. The Belgian goalkeeper believes his Real Madrid teammate deserves recognition for his individual performances, although he acknowledged that Lamine Yamal has the advantage of having won major trophies with Barcelona and Spain. Courtois throws his weight behind Mbappe “I think Kylian deserves it, but people vote according to their own logic,” Courtois told DAZN (h/t AS ), just days before the Ballon d’Or ceremony, which will take place in London next Monday. Courtois highlighted the dilemma between rewarding individual performances and collective succes, saying: “Do we choose someone who has won trophies, or someone who has been above everyone else throughout the season, even if they have not won anything? “I am thinking especially of Kylian. I think individually nobody has been better than Kylian, but unfortunately, we have not won anything collectively.” One of the contenders for Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The Belgian recalled that Mbappe finished fourth at the World Cup and was the tournament’s top scorer, while his main rival for the award, Lamine Yamal, became world champion with Spain. “For me, Lamine Yamal had a slightly worse World Cup, but he became world champion, won La Liga with Barcelona and had a good year,” said the 34-year-old goalkeeper. Courtois also questioned the voting criteria, recalling that he expected Vinicius Jr. or Dani Carvajal to win the 2024 award, only for Spain midfielder Rodri to take the prize. “I did not think it had been his best year, although he won the European Championship with Spain. The previous year, when City won the Champions League, I think he would have deserved to win it,” Courtois said. He added that “sometimes it is difficult to know how to vote for the Ballon d’Or”. Contract renewal at Real Madrid Turning to his future at Real Madrid, Courtois said he expects to finalise a contract extension soon. His current deal expires in June 2027, with an agreement for another year understood to be close . “It is not finalised yet. In principle, it should be resolved quickly. There is no problem. We simply need to find time for my agent and my father to discuss the final details,” he explained. “I want to stay here for a long time, and I am doing everything I can to make that happen,” he added. Courtois will sign a new contract until 2028. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images) Belgium situation Courtois also revealed that he has been removed from the Belgium national team players’ WhatsApp group, following his decision to take a break from international football after the World Cup. However, he played down the situation, explaining that he remains in contact with some team-mates and is hopeful of representing the Red Devils again. “I have been kicked out of the players’ WhatsApp group. That group is used to communicate information, such as training details. There are a few messages from time to time, but not that many,” he said. The goalkeeper expressed optimism about Belgium’s future under new head coach Mark van Bommel, the Dutchman who has taken charge of the national team. “Everyone was fairly satisfied after the first international camp. The team is heading in the right direction, as is the coach. This national team has a great future,” Courtois said. Having considered retiring from international football after the 2026 World Cup, Courtois explained that the positive atmosphere during the tournament changed his mind. He also revealed that he had offered Van Bommel a compromise by making himself available to return to the national team in November. Courtois stressed that he does not expect guarantees of a starting place, once he returns. “I have never reported for international duty assuming I would automatically play. I know my qualities and I know I can be important to the team,” he said. “Nobody needs to guarantee me a starting place. If Senne Lammens, Maarten Vandevoordt or Mike Penders have worked hard and the coach prefers to play them, there is no problem. It does not bother me at all,” he added.

item.title: Newcastle wants to beat Juventus to English defender
item.description: Newcastle wants to beat Juventus to English defender Juventus were keen to sign Fikayo Tomori during the summer before deciding to pursue Jhon Lucumi instead. However, the Bianconeri remain interested in the AC Milan defender, particularly with his contract situation potentially allowing them to sign him as a free agent. Tomori remains an experienced centre back who has established himself in Serie A. His quality and familiarity with Italian football make him an attractive option for Juventus as they consider ways to strengthen their defence. However, Juventus are not the only club monitoring his situation. With the possibility of signing him without paying a transfer fee, several teams could compete for his signature, making the race more difficult for the Italian giants. Newcastle enter the race for Tomori According to Football Insider , Newcastle United are the latest club to show interest in signing Tomori. The Premier League side reportedly views the defender as one of their leading transfer targets for the summer and would be keen to persuade him to return to England. A move back to the Premier League could appeal to Tomori, who would have the opportunity to continue his career in familiar surroundings. Newcastle could also offer a competitive financial package if he becomes available as a free agent. Juventus would therefore need to make an attractive proposal to remain in contention. Although they have tracked the defender for some time, their interest alone will not guarantee that he chooses to continue playing in Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images) Juventus face competition for his signature The prospect of signing Tomori without a transfer fee makes him an appealing target for both clubs. Juventus could strengthen their defensive options without paying Milan a transfer fee, but they may have to compete financially with Newcastle to secure an agreement. The Bianconeri remain capable of winning the race, provided they can offer terms that satisfy the defender. However, Newcastle’s interest could complicate their plans, particularly if the English club makes a serious effort to bring him home. Newcastle’s own season has been turbulent, and their final league position remains uncertain. That could influence their transfer plans and their ability to attract targets. For Juventus, Tomori remains a potential opportunity, but the club must be prepared for competition. If Newcastle pursue him aggressively, the financial terms and sporting project offered by both sides could prove decisive in determining his next destination.

item.title: Roma’s Champions League earnings reach €52 million
item.description: Roma’s Champions League earnings reach €52 million Roma are back on track in the Champions League, and financially, too. After losing to José Mourinho’s Real Madrid, Gian Piero Gasperini’s side swept Slovan Bratislava 4-0, securing their first win of the League Phase. This result allows the Giallorossi to climb to four points in the standings, following their opening draw against Fenerbahçe. More importantly, their European success guarantees the club an immediate bonus of €2.1 million, in addition to the €700,000 already earned on Matchday 1. Participation in Europe’s premier competition represents a particularly significant source of revenue for the Roman club. According to Calcio e Finanza estimates, Roma has already reached €52.19 million in total revenue from the 2026-2027 Champions League. This sum is made up of several components, starting with the €18.62 million guaranteed simply by qualifying for the league phase. Added to these are the 2.8 million earned through on-field results and a minimum share of 275 thousand euros tied to the final placing.

item.title: Real Betis midfielder Facundo Bernal slapped with heavy ban after 'headbutt' assault on Barcelona star Lamine Yamal
item.description: Real Betis Balompie v FC Barcelona - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Real Betis midfielder Facundo Bernal has been slapped with a four-game suspension following a fiery clash with Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal. The Uruguayan was sent off after headbutting the teenager during a dramatic 5-2 defeat at the weekend. Big suspension confirmed Bernal has been given a four-game ban by the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) disciplinary committee on Wednesday. The sanction comes following his sending off during a 5-2 defeat against Barca at the weekend. Bernal was sent off in the 54th minute, shortly after Betis scored to narrow the deficit to 3-2. His dismissal completely swung the momentum of the high-stakes match back in favor of the opposition. The 23-year-old midfielder will now face an extended period on the sidelines. His actions have drawn severe disciplinary consequences from the Spanish governing body. Clash with Lamine Yamal The disciplinary report published on Wednesday by the RFEF outlined the specific reasons behind the harsh punishment. According to the official report, Bernal grabbed Yamal by the neck before headbutting him twice. The Uruguayan international was deemed to have assaulted Yamal while the ball was not in play. The governing body's disciplinary code strictly dictates that bans range from four to 12 games for such violent behaviour. Bernal ultimately received the minimum penalty permitted under the regulations for the offense. Yamal was also booked during the heated exchange for pushing the Betis midfielder prior to the red-card incident. Real Betis Balompie v FC Barcelona - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 More disciplinary trouble The match unravelled completely for Betis following the red card. Barca capitalised on the numerical advantage to score three unanswered goals, with Yamal assisting Gabriel Jesus for the third effort. The fallout extended beyond the pitch as well. Betis sporting director Manu Fajardo was also sanctioned with a two-game suspension and a fine for conduct contrary to good sporting order. Key matches missed Bernal will miss a crucial run of Liga fixtures for Betis. He is set to sit out upcoming matches against Celta Vigo, Malaga, Elche, and the fierce derby clash with Sevilla on November 22. The suspension serves as a significant blow to the squad's midfield depth during a crucial phase of the campaign. Betis currently sit fourth in the Liga standings on 19 points.

item.title: Van Dijk says 'risk' is worth reward under Liverpool boss Iraola
item.description: Villarreal's Nathan-Dylan Saliba (R) and Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk battle for the ball during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Liverpool FC and Villarreal CF at Anfield. (is associated with: «Van Dijk says 'risk' is worth reward under Liverpool boss Iraola») Nick Potts/PA Wire/dpa Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk believes the risks associated with playing Andoni Iraola's way is worth the reward - although it helps when you have a teenage winger as exciting as Rio Ngumoha. Villarreal exposed the spaces and flaws in a team showing six changes to take a 2-0 lead inside 30 minutes at Anfield on Tuesday but, inspired by their 18-year-old phenomenon, the hosts fought back to win 4-3 to maintain their 100% Champions League record. The change involved Iraola doubling-down on his high-intensity pressing in the second half, gambling on a man-to-man approach to first nullify the visitors' superior mobility and then turn the game in their favour. Ngumoha's pace and directness was a key factor but the positivity of bringing on Florian Wirtz at half-time and dropping previous number 10 Ryan Gravenberch to right-back was rewarded with a third successive win. It was the first time Liverpool had come from 2-0 down to win in the Champions League since beating Villarreal in the 2022 semi-final. "Obviously we don't want to put ourselves in a position where you have to come back from anything and that's what I did from the start," said Van Dijk, who was at pains to take responsibility for "a bad day at the office" after his individual error led to conceding the first goal. "It wasn't a great first half but we got it turned around. When it pays off, yes definitely (it's exciting). "But when you just mistime the tackle or when they flick it then it could be wide open but that was definitely the message: we have to go all-in if we try to win the ball up high and you have to take that risk and second half we were much better." Ngumoha was deservedly awarded man of the match as, in addition to his two assists for Alexis Mac Allister, he was, in Van Dijk's words, "pretty electric". The 18-year-old has completed more successful dribbles (16) than any player in the Champions League, with Barcelona's Ballon d'Or contender Lamine Yamal four behind in second place. "He was a complete threat constantly and their defender had a tough time," added Van Dijk, who believes spending last season in the same squad as Mohamed Salah was of huge benefit. "Everyone is chipping in but for him to work with Mo last year was obviously massive as Mo was one of the best wingers at the club and experienced everything, so why not soak in all the information and show it on the pitch and show your own qualities? "I think he has shown it this season but there is still much more to come."

item.title: What are the EFL rules on homegrown players?
item.description: Watford are among the clubs who have a number of homegrown players that do not represent England or Wales [Getty Images] In the Championship, League One and League Two, clubs must have a minimum of eight homegrown players registered in their squad. For a league game in the EFL, clubs must name at least seven homegrown players in their matchday squad. A homegrown player is someone who has been registered with either their current club, or any English or Welsh club, for a period of three seasons or 36 months prior to either their 21st birthday, or the end of the season that the player in question turns 21. These rules are only enforced in league matches and are not enforced by the EFL for the FA Cup, EFL Cup or EFL Trophy. The Premier League operates its own separate system of rules on squad lists and homegrown players. An example of the rule classifying players as homegrown, despite not being English or Welsh, can be seen in Watford's recent 2-0 win over Charlton Athletic. Watford defenders Mattie Pollock and Marc Bola were the only players who are listed as English in the Hornets matchday squad. However, Hector Kyprianou (Cyprus), Jordan Zemura (Zimbabwe), Daniel Bachmann (Austria), Stephy Mavididi (Democratic Republic of Congo) and Amin Nabizada (Afghanistan), who all represent other countries for international games, are classed as homegrown due to where they played their club football as youth players. Once an EFL club has submitted its squad list following the conclusion of the summer transfer window, each club is required to list at least one club-developed player per match on its squad list or team sheet. For any match in which a club fails to do so, they are permitted one fewer player on their bench for the game. In the Championship, that would mean eight substitutes instead of nine, and in League One and League Two, it would result in six substitutes instead of seven. Players aged under 21 do not count towards squad lists across all three EFL leagues, while goalkeepers are not included in the squad lists for League One and League Two. This article is the latest from BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team. This question is from James in London. More questions answered... Why are some football shin pads so small?

item.title: Troy Aikman made his disdain of analytics known on ‘Monday Night Football’
item.description: Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Troy Aikman’s ESPN future is uncertain , but for this NFL season, Aikman is still in the Monday Night Football booth with Joe Buck, and he’s delivering commentary with the utmost certainty. This Monday, during the San Francisco 49ers’ win over the Washington Commanders, Buck disclosed that 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan has “talked about analytics a lot with us.” “He said it’s in the equation, but [he’s] been been calling plays for almost 20 years in this league, and there’s a lot of gut feel that he uses in spots like this,” Buck said, referencing San Francisco facing a fourth-and-3 in the first quarter. “Yeah, I agree,” Aikman said, “and I think analytics is a good way to lose your job as a head coach. I think you’ve got to be smart about it. Kyle certainly is. The analytics, by the way, does say go for it, but as you mention, it’s not something that Kyle Shanahan always pays that much attention to. More gut than anything else.” Aikman’s analytics take hit the radar of many Monday Night Football viewers, and they vented about it on Twitter. “It’s not a Troy Aikman broadcast until he sh*ts on analytics,” JJ Zachariason wrote . item.title: Browns Insider Reveals Potential Trade Deadline Plans After Surprising 4-2 Start
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Sue Levine, Editor Nobody expected the Cleveland Browns to be shopping for reinforcements in late October. Not after trading Myles Garrett . Not with a new head coach and a roster that appeared headed for another rebuilding year. Yet Cleveland is 4-2, leading the AFC North, and its trade deadline plans may have taken an unexpected turn. Longtime Browns reporter Mary Kay Cabot believes Cleveland will be looking to add players before November 10th. She even has a particular veteran in mind. Browns Trade Deadline Plans Could Bring a Familiar Name Into the Picture During Tuesday’s Orange and Brown Talk podcast , Cabot was asked whether Cleveland might be buying or selling at the deadline. Her answer wasn’t particularly complicated. “Yes, I do think they will be buyers as they approach the trade deadline,” Cabot said. “I think they are more apt to be buyers than sellers.” Six weeks ago, that would have sounded ridiculous. The Browns had just moved on from Garrett, their best defensive player, and nobody was penciling them in for a division title. Now they’re ahead of Baltimore, Pittsburgh, and Cincinnati. Cabot also mentioned Khalil Mack as a player Cleveland should consider pursuing. The Los Angeles Chargers are winless through six games. Mack is 35 years old, and a rebuilding team might have little reason to hold onto an expensive veteran if another club offers reasonable compensation. Cabot floated the possibility of acquiring him for a fifth-round pick. That’s her suggested valuation; however, not a reported asking price from Los Angeles. There’s also no indication that the Browns and Chargers have discussed a deal. Even so, Mack’s inclusion in the conversation makes Cleveland’s trade deadline plans worth following. Cleveland’s Trade Deadline Plans Shouldn’t Ignore the Offense There’s one problem with the idea of adding another pass rusher. The Browns can barely score. Through six games , Cleveland is averaging 17.7 points. That isn’t exactly an offense striking fear into opposing defensive coordinators. The defense has done enough to keep the team competitive. Asking that unit to continue carrying such a heavy burden, especially as the schedule gets deeper into November and December, seems like a dangerous gamble. So why not use those trade deadline plans to find another offensive weapon? The offensive line could certainly benefit from additional depth. Injuries have also created questions in the backfield, leaving Cleveland with some uncomfortable decisions about how to support its running game. Mack would be an exciting acquisition. Nobody would complain about another proven pass rusher joining the defense. But would he fix the team’s biggest weakness? Probably not. Berry has to consider that before making any changes to his trade deadline plans. Cleveland doesn’t need to win the transaction headlines. It needs to find ways to score more points. item.content:encoded: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Sue Levine, Editor Nobody expected the Cleveland Browns to be shopping for reinforcements in late October. Not after trading Myles Garrett . Not with a new head coach and a roster that appeared headed for another rebuilding year. Yet Cleveland is 4-2, leading the AFC North, and its trade deadline plans may have taken an unexpected turn. Longtime Browns reporter Mary Kay Cabot believes Cleveland will be looking to add players before November 10th. She even has a particular veteran in mind. Browns Trade Deadline Plans Could Bring a Familiar Name Into the Picture During Tuesday’s Orange and Brown Talk podcast , Cabot was asked whether Cleveland might be buying or selling at the deadline. Her answer wasn’t particularly complicated. “Yes, I do think they will be buyers as they approach the trade deadline,” Cabot said. “I think they are more apt to be buyers than sellers.” Six weeks ago, that would have sounded ridiculous. The Browns had just moved on from Garrett, their best defensive player, and nobody was penciling them in for a division title. Now they’re ahead of Baltimore, Pittsburgh, and Cincinnati. Cabot also mentioned Khalil Mack as a player Cleveland should consider pursuing. The Los Angeles Chargers are winless through six games. Mack is 35 years old, and a rebuilding team might have little reason to hold onto an expensive veteran if another club offers reasonable compensation. Cabot floated the possibility of acquiring him for a fifth-round pick. That’s her suggested valuation; however, not a reported asking price from Los Angeles. There’s also no indication that the Browns and Chargers have discussed a deal. Even so, Mack’s inclusion in the conversation makes Cleveland’s trade deadline plans worth following. Cleveland’s Trade Deadline Plans Shouldn’t Ignore the Offense There’s one problem with the idea of adding another pass rusher. The Browns can barely score. Through six games , Cleveland is averaging 17.7 points. That isn’t exactly an offense striking fear into opposing defensive coordinators. The defense has done enough to keep the team competitive. Asking that unit to continue carrying such a heavy burden, especially as the schedule gets deeper into November and December, seems like a dangerous gamble. So why not use those trade deadline plans to find another offensive weapon? The offensive line could certainly benefit from additional depth. Injuries have also created questions in the backfield, leaving Cleveland with some uncomfortable decisions about how to support its running game. Mack would be an exciting acquisition. Nobody would complain about another proven pass rusher joining the defense. But would he fix the team’s biggest weakness? Probably not. Berry has to consider that before making any changes to his trade deadline plans. Cleveland doesn’t need to win the transaction headlines. It needs to find ways to score more points. Andrew Berry Faces an Unusual Decision The Garrett trade left Cleveland with additional draft capital, including the Rams’ 2027 first-round selection. That gives Berry options. It doesn’t mean he should start throwing picks around. There’s a difference between surrendering a fifth-rounder for a veteran who can contribute immediately and giving away premium draft capital because the team unexpectedly won four games. The Browns’ trade deadline plans should account for both possibilities: Cleveland might have a legitimate playoff opportunity, but it still has a roster that needs work. Todd Monken deserves credit for getting this group to 4-2. Few expected that kind of start. Still, six games aren’t enough to erase the questions surrounding the franchise. One injury, a couple of bad offensive performances, or a difficult stretch against division opponents could change the outlook quickly. That’s the uncomfortable position Berry finds himself in. Stick with the roster and risk wasting an opportunity? Or make a move and potentially sacrifice resources that the organization spent the offseason accumulating? Those aren’t decisions Cleveland expected to face this soon. Oct 18, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III (9) rushes as Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Khalil Mack (52) tackles during the fourth quarter at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: William Purnell-Imagn Images The Last Word Cabot’s comments have made the Browns’ trade deadline plans considerably more interesting. Cleveland entered the season looking like a team preparing for the future. Now there’s a legitimate reason to consider helping the present. Mack would be a fascinating addition, particularly if the price were as reasonable as Cabot suggested. But the offense needs attention, and Berry shouldn’t overlook that simply because a recognizable defensive player might become available. The Browns have already accomplished more than many expected through six games. Whether they’re legitimate contenders is another question entirely. Their trade deadline plans won’t answer everything, but they’ll provide a pretty good indication of how seriously Cleveland’s front office is taking this unexpected opportunity. item.title: Delta youths seize Macaraba oil field over alleged marginalization
item.description: By Jimitota Onoyume Hundreds of youths from Ifie-Kporo community in Warri South local government area of Delta state yesterday (today Wednesday) shut down operations at the Macaraba oil field, accusing the operating firm of marginalising the community and refusing to recognise it as a host community. The protesters, who arrived at the field in speedboats, demanded justice, youth employment, and recognition of the community’s rights over Wells 24 and 25. They carried placards with several inscriptions which included , “We Want Justice,” “Employ Our Youths,” and “Give Us Our Rights or Leave Our Land.” The youths accused the oil firm of operating on their ancestral land without adequately recognising or engaging the community, vowing to remain at the field until their grievances are addressed. Speaking during the protest, one of the youths, who gave his name as Tosan, said the company had been unfair to the community and warned that the occupation would continue until their demands were met. The protesters insisted that Wells 24 and 25 sit on Ifie-Kporo ancestral land and urged the firm to respect their rights as a host community in line with the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA). They called on the company to follow the precedent set by Gulf, which they said had recognised and engaged with the community as host to its oil facilities. The youths warned that continued neglect of their demands could threaten peace in the area, and urged the firm to resolve the dispute through dialogue rather than allow the situation to escalate. The post Delta youths seize Macaraba oil field over alleged marginalization appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 5 things to know about Chinese AI startup DeepSeek
item.description: The United States Department of Homeland Security ordered government agencies on Monday to stop using artificial intelligence tools from DeepSeek, citing concerns over data being transferred to China. Here are five things to know about the Chinese AI startup following the new restrictions: – ‘Sputnik moment’ – Founded by Liang Wenfeng in the eastern Chinese tech hub Hangzhou, DeepSeek started life in 2023 as a side project of Liang’s data-driven hedge fund that had access to a cache of powerful AI processors made by US chip giant Nvidia. It gained global attention in January 2025 with the release of its R1 deep-reasoning large language model, which sparked a US tech share sell-off. Industry insiders were stunned by R1’s high performance — at a level similar to ChatGPT and other leading US chatbots — and DeepSeek’s claims to have developed it at a fraction of the cost. Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen described it as a “Sputnik moment”, referencing the 1957 launch of Earth’s first artificial satellite by the Soviet Union that stunned the Western world. – Censorship concerns – Like other Chinese chatbots, DeepSeek’s AI tools eschew topics usually censored in the world’s second-largest economy, such as the 1989 Tiananmen crackdown. That and data privacy concerns have led DeepSeek AI to be banned or restricted on government-issued devices in several countries, including the United States, Australia and South Korea. On Monday, the US went further by banning civilian government agencies from using products developed by DeepSeek and third-party tools created using DeepSeek. China’s foreign ministry said it opposed that move and accused the US of “overstretching” the concept of national security. DeepSeek’s low cost and ease of deployment have made it a popular choice in developing countries, analysts say. The company holds around four percent of global market share for chatbots, according to web traffic analysis company Similarweb. ChatGPT dominates at 68 percent. – Open source – DeepSeek’s systems are open-source, meaning their inner workings are public, allowing programmers to customise parts of the software to suit their needs. That is the same for other major Chinese AI players, including tech giant Alibaba, in contrast to the “closed” models sold by OpenAI and other Western rivals. The Chinese government has trumpeted its lead in open-source AI technology, which it says can accelerate innovation. “Chinese AI models are leading the way in the open-source innovation ecosystem,” National People’s Congress spokesman Lou Qinjian told policymakers in April. – Startup boost – The success of DeepSeek has galvanised China’s AI scene, despite hurdles posed by rivalry with the United States and fears of a global market bubble. Shares in two leading Chinese AI startups, Zhipu AI and MiniMax, soared on their market debuts in Hong Kong this year, and it has been a similar story for Chinese chipmakers such as MetaX. item.content:encoded: The United States Department of Homeland Security ordered government agencies on Monday to stop using artificial intelligence tools from DeepSeek, citing concerns over data being transferred to China. Here are five things to know about the Chinese AI startup following the new restrictions: – ‘Sputnik moment’ – Founded by Liang Wenfeng in the eastern Chinese tech hub Hangzhou, DeepSeek started life in 2023 as a side project of Liang’s data-driven hedge fund that had access to a cache of powerful AI processors made by US chip giant Nvidia. It gained global attention in January 2025 with the release of its R1 deep-reasoning large language model, which sparked a US tech share sell-off. Industry insiders were stunned by R1’s high performance — at a level similar to ChatGPT and other leading US chatbots — and DeepSeek’s claims to have developed it at a fraction of the cost. Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen described it as a “Sputnik moment”, referencing the 1957 launch of Earth’s first artificial satellite by the Soviet Union that stunned the Western world. – Censorship concerns – Like other Chinese chatbots, DeepSeek’s AI tools eschew topics usually censored in the world’s second-largest economy, such as the 1989 Tiananmen crackdown. That and data privacy concerns have led DeepSeek AI to be banned or restricted on government-issued devices in several countries, including the United States, Australia and South Korea. On Monday, the US went further by banning civilian government agencies from using products developed by DeepSeek and third-party tools created using DeepSeek. China’s foreign ministry said it opposed that move and accused the US of “overstretching” the concept of national security. DeepSeek’s low cost and ease of deployment have made it a popular choice in developing countries, analysts say. The company holds around four percent of global market share for chatbots, according to web traffic analysis company Similarweb. ChatGPT dominates at 68 percent. – Open source – DeepSeek’s systems are open-source, meaning their inner workings are public, allowing programmers to customise parts of the software to suit their needs. That is the same for other major Chinese AI players, including tech giant Alibaba, in contrast to the “closed” models sold by OpenAI and other Western rivals. The Chinese government has trumpeted its lead in open-source AI technology, which it says can accelerate innovation. “Chinese AI models are leading the way in the open-source innovation ecosystem,” National People’s Congress spokesman Lou Qinjian told policymakers in April. – Startup boost – The success of DeepSeek has galvanised China’s AI scene, despite hurdles posed by rivalry with the United States and fears of a global market bubble. Shares in two leading Chinese AI startups, Zhipu AI and MiniMax, soared on their market debuts in Hong Kong this year, and it has been a similar story for Chinese chipmakers such as MetaX. In June, investors valued DeepSeek at more than $50 billion in the company’s first funding round, according to the Wall Street Journal. Shi Yaqiong and her team at Beijing-based Jinqiu Capital told AFP there has been a “clear surge” in enthusiasm around Chinese AI — and competition among investors — since the DeepSeek shock. – Chip smuggling reports – DeepSeek’s rise has not been without controversy. Reports, including in technology outlet The Information, say DeepSeek has been skirting a US ban on the export of top-end chips to China to train its new V4 model. The Information said in December, citing six people with knowledge of the matter, that DeepSeek developed V4 using thousands of chips dismantled in third countries and smuggled to China. DeepSeek did not respond to AFP’s request for comment at the time. Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment but told The Information that they had not seen any evidence of this and that “such smuggling seems farfetched”. In April, DeepSeek said it had used both Nvidia and Huawei’s domestically-produced Ascend chips for its new model. Huawei, at the forefront of Chinese efforts to reduce reliance on US semiconductor technology, said in a statement that the full range of its Ascend products support DeepSeek’s V4 series. Washington says DeepSeek’s latest model is about eight months behind the top offerings from US companies. item.title: Toulouse v Troyes Ligue 1 game postponed as France gripped by unrest
item.description: The Ligue 1 match between Toulouse and Troyes this weekend has has pushed back a day at the request of local authorities struggling to contain unrest in France, the French league (LFP) announced on Wednesday. The match which had been due to take place in Toulouse in southwest France at 1715 local time (1515 GMT) on Saturday will now kick off on Sunday at the same time. “Although not considered high-risk, organising an event with such a large turnout requires the deployment of internal security forces and municipal police personnel,” the Haute-Garonne prefecture, which manages public services and security in the region, said. A second sporting event is also scheduled in Toulouse on Saturday with the city’s rugby club set to host Perpignan in a Top 14 rugby match. On Tuesday, the Ligue 2 match between Montpellier and Paris-based Red Star originally scheduled for Saturday was moved to Monday. Some of the worst urban violence to hit France in years erupted last Saturday on the fringe of nationwide protests over the rising cost of living. Since then, authorities have ordered partial curfews in parts of Paris and other cities, including Toulouse, to prevent further violence. There was tight security at the Parc des Princes in Paris on Tuesday for Paris Saint-Germain’s victory against Barcelona in the Champions League. PSG will host Lyon at the same venue in a Ligue 1 match on Sunday evening. The post Toulouse v Troyes Ligue 1 game postponed as France gripped by unrest appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Yamal breaks into 10 highest paid footballers in the world [Full list]
item.description: Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal has been ranked sixth among the world’s highest-paid footballers in 2026, with estimated earnings of $55 million, according to Forbes. Cristiano Ronaldo tops the ranking with $300 million, followed by Lionel Messi with $145 million and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé with $100 million. Forbes estimates that the 10 highest-paid footballers will earn a combined $942 million this season, with Ronaldo and Messi accounting for nearly half of the total. Below is the list of the world’s 10 highest-paid footballers in 2026, according to Forbes. 1. Cristiano Ronaldo — $300 million The Al Nassr forward leads the ranking with estimated earnings of $300 million, comprising $250 million from football and $50 million from endorsements and other business ventures. The 41-year-old Portugal captain has built a commercial portfolio that includes his CR7 brand, hotels and investments in several businesses. 2. Lionel Messi — $145 million Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi ranks second with estimated earnings of $145 million. The Argentine earns about $70 million on the pitch and $75 million from endorsements and other off-field ventures, including partnerships with major global brands. 3. Kylian Mbappé — $100 million Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé occupies third place with estimated earnings of $100 million. His income includes $70 million from football and $30 million from commercial partnerships. The France international has also expanded his business interests through a new partnership with Swiss sportswear brand On. 4. Erling Haaland — $85 million Manchester City striker Erling Haaland ranks fourth with estimated earnings of $85 million. The Norway international is projected to earn $60 million from football and $25 million from endorsements. His commercial partners include Nike and digital bank Revolut. 5. Vinicius Jr. — $76 million Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr. ranks fifth with estimated earnings of $76 million. The Brazilian is expected to earn $48 million on the pitch and $28 million off it through endorsements and commercial partnerships with brands including Hugo Boss and Fanatics. 6. Lamine Yamal — $55 million Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal ranks sixth with estimated earnings of $55 million, comprising $35 million from football and $20 million from endorsements. The 19-year-old Spain international has attracted growing commercial attention following his performances for Barcelona and Spain. His sponsors include American Eagle, Coca-Cola and McDonald’s. American Eagle signed Yamal to a five-year deal, marking its first multi-year partnership with an athlete. 7. Sadio Mané — $54 million Al Nassr winger Sadio Mané ranks seventh with estimated earnings of $54 million. The Senegal international is projected to earn $50 million from football and $4 million from endorsements. His commercial portfolio includes a long-term partnership with sportswear brand New Balance. 8. Jude Bellingham — $45 million Real Madrid midfielder Jude B
