The Senegal international is projected to earn $50 million from football and $4 million from endorsements. His commercial portfolio includes a long-term partnership with sportswear brand New Balance. 8. Jude Bellingham — $45 million Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham occupies eighth place with estimated earnings of $45 million. The England international is expected to earn $29 million on the pitch and $16 million from endorsements and other commercial activities. His partners include Adidas, Louis Vuitton and Skims. 9. Harry Kane — $42 million Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane ranks ninth with estimated earnings of $42 million. The England captain is projected to earn $29 million from football and $13 million off the pitch. His commercial partnerships include sportswear brand Skechers, Google Gemini and Oura Ring. 10. Mohamed Salah — $40 million Egyptian forward Mohamed Salah completes the top 10 with estimated earnings of $40 million. The former Liverpool star is projected to earn $20 million from football and another $20 million from endorsements. His commercial partners include Adidas, Pepsi and Vodafone. The ranking highlights the financial dominance of Ronaldo and Messi, while the inclusion of younger stars such as Yamal, Mbappé, Haaland and Bellingham points to the next generation of football’s biggest commercial names. item.title: Visual artist Amadeo Carvalho explores Black identity
item.description: From Cape Verde to London and beyond, Amadeo Carvalho is a self-taught, London-based contemporary visual artist putting Black identity, memory and heritage at the heart of his work. Blending painting, poetry and photography, his art explores the stories, silences and connections that shape who we are. This weekend, his powerful collection "Portraits of Absence" arrives at the AKAA Art Fair here in Paris, where it will be exhibited by the curatorial platform Casa Vicência. He spoke to us in Perspective

item.title: Jonathan urges Nigeria to shift from imports to production
item.description: By Soni Daniel ABUJA — Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called on Nigeria to develop the resources and technology needed to produce goods and services locally rather than continue to depend on imports. Jonathan made the call on Wednesday while commissioning the Zeetin Technologies plant in Idu, Abuja, which manufactures tricycles for the Nigerian market. He said Nigeria’s large youth population could serve as a major asset in boosting local production, creating economic opportunities and driving national development. The former president urged Nigeria to emulate countries that had successfully mobilised their resources and young populations to expand their manufacturing capacity and become reliable producers and exporters of goods. He stressed the need for Nigeria to harness its human and material resources to strengthen domestic production and reduce dependence on imported goods. The post Jonathan urges Nigeria to shift from imports to production appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Toluwanisings’ family announces service of songs, seeks support for widow, children
item.description: The family of late Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has announced a night of tributes and service of songs in his honour while appealing to the public for financial support for his wife and children. The event is scheduled for Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at 3pm at the Hall of Grace, Jogor Centre, Ibadan, Oyo State. The family announced the programme in a post on the singer’s social media page, inviting friends, colleagues, fans and well-wishers to celebrate his life and ministry. “We invite you to join us for a Night of Tributes and Service of Songs in honour of our beloved brother, friend, and gospel minister, Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, fondly known as Toluwanisings,” the statement read. In a separate appeal titled “A Call for Love and Support,” the family urged Nigerians to assist the singer’s wife and children following his death on October 14. The family called on well-meaning individuals to contribute towards supporting the widow as she navigates life after the loss of her husband. “As we mourn the loss of our beloved brother, let us stand with his wife during this difficult season. Every contribution, no matter how small, is a gesture of love and compassion,” the family said. It also provided account details for donations and prayed for blessings on those willing to support the bereaved family. “Please support her through the account details provided. May God bless every giving heart and grant the family strength and comfort,” the statement added. Toluwanisings died on October 14, 2026, hours after ministering at a praise concert organised by fellow gospel singer Bidemi Olaoba in Ibadan. His death sparked widespread reactions on social media, with questions raised about access to emergency medical care after his personal assistant alleged that several hospitals refused to admit him. The planned night of tributes and service of songs will provide an opportunity for family members, friends, colleagues and fans to honour the late singer’s life and musical contributions. The post Toluwanisings’ family announces service of songs, seeks support for widow, children appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ebola: Ogun steps up surveillance, says no case recorded in state
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State government has intensified surveillance and preparedness measures following the Federal Government’s announcement of an Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), assuring residents that no case had been recorded in the state . The government urged residents to remain vigilant, observe preventive measures and avoid panic or the spread of unverified information. The State Commissioner for Health, Dr. Tomi Coker, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, noting that Ogun had been on heightened alert since the declaration of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in March 2026. According to her, 111 persons of interest, comprising passengers from high-risk countries, had been identified, monitored and subsequently discharged from follow-up after completing the required surveillance period. Coker said the state’s Public Health Emergency Operations Centre was coordinating preparedness and response activities to ensure the prompt identification, reporting and management of any suspected case. She added that the government had strengthened the capacity of Disease Surveillance and Notification Officers, port health officers, health educators, clinicians and community informants through training on appropriate response procedures. The commissioner said relevant national guidelines, protocols and resource materials had been adapted and deployed to guide the state’s response, while public sensitisation and infection prevention and control measures in healthcare facilities were being intensified. She urged residents to remain calm and obtain information from official public health authorities. Coker explained that Ebola is a serious disease that can cause severe illness and death, noting that its early symptoms may resemble those of other common illnesses. She listed the symptoms to include fever, severe weakness, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal pain. Unexplained bleeding or bruising may also occur in some cases. According to her, symptoms can develop between two and 21 days after exposure. She stressed, however, that experiencing these symptoms does not automatically mean a person has Ebola, although prompt professional assessment is essential, particularly where there has been possible exposure or travel to a high-risk area. The commissioner explained that Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person who has developed symptoms, the body of someone who has died from the disease, or materials contaminated with such fluids. item.dc:creator: Urowayino Jeremiah
item.content:encoded: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State government has intensified surveillance and preparedness measures following the Federal Government’s announcement of an Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), assuring residents that no case had been recorded in the state . The government urged residents to remain vigilant, observe preventive measures and avoid panic or the spread of unverified information. The State Commissioner for Health, Dr. Tomi Coker, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, noting that Ogun had been on heightened alert since the declaration of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in March 2026. According to her, 111 persons of interest, comprising passengers from high-risk countries, had been identified, monitored and subsequently discharged from follow-up after completing the required surveillance period. Coker said the state’s Public Health Emergency Operations Centre was coordinating preparedness and response activities to ensure the prompt identification, reporting and management of any suspected case. She added that the government had strengthened the capacity of Disease Surveillance and Notification Officers, port health officers, health educators, clinicians and community informants through training on appropriate response procedures. The commissioner said relevant national guidelines, protocols and resource materials had been adapted and deployed to guide the state’s response, while public sensitisation and infection prevention and control measures in healthcare facilities were being intensified. She urged residents to remain calm and obtain information from official public health authorities. Coker explained that Ebola is a serious disease that can cause severe illness and death, noting that its early symptoms may resemble those of other common illnesses. She listed the symptoms to include fever, severe weakness, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal pain. Unexplained bleeding or bruising may also occur in some cases. According to her, symptoms can develop between two and 21 days after exposure. She stressed, however, that experiencing these symptoms does not automatically mean a person has Ebola, although prompt professional assessment is essential, particularly where there has been possible exposure or travel to a high-risk area. The commissioner explained that Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person who has developed symptoms, the body of someone who has died from the disease, or materials contaminated with such fluids. She advised residents to wash their hands regularly with soap and running water and use alcohol-based hand sanitiser when soap and water are unavailable. Residents were also cautioned against contact with the blood and body fluids of anyone suspected of having the disease and sharing needles, razors or other items that could be contaminated. Coker urged anyone who might have been exposed to Ebola to contact public health authorities promptly without waiting for symptoms to develop. She further advised anyone who develops symptoms after possible exposure to avoid close contact with others and contact public health authorities before visiting a healthcare facility, to enable safe referral to an appropriate medical centre. The commissioner also called on residents to cooperate with surveillance and follow-up teams, provide accurate information when contacted by public health officials and comply with the guidance issued. She warned against touching the bodies of people who die from suspected or confirmed Ebola, stressing that safe and dignified burials must be handled by trained teams. Coker also cautioned against rumours, discrimination and stigmatisation, urging residents to share only information from verified public health sources. She said the Ogun State Government would continue to work with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) and other relevant partners to monitor developments and implement appropriate measures to protect public health. The commissioner called on healthcare workers in public and private facilities to maintain a high index of suspicion, promptly identify and isolate suspected cases, observe strict infection prevention and control protocols, and immediately notify the state surveillance team through the Disease Surveillance and Notification Officers in their respective local government areas. She provided the contact number of the State Epidemiologist as 08084250881 and the NCDC toll-free line as 6232 for reporting suspected cases and obtaining public health guidance. Coker emphasised that early detection, timely reporting and cooperation among residents, healthcare workers and public health authorities were essential to preventing the spread of the disease. item.title: Suspected kidnappers kill 7-year-old boy hours after demanding N2.5m ransom in Jos
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos A seven-year-old boy, Abdullahi Rabi’u, has been found dead hours after suspected kidnappers abducted him and demanded a ransom of N2.5 million in Majema area, along Ring Road, Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The victim’s uncle, Sukairaj Danladi Gado, who narrated the incident, said the boy was sent on an errand to a neighbour’s house on Monday evening but failed to return after delivering the message. “The family became worried when Abdullahi did not return home. We made efforts to locate him, but all our efforts proved abortive,” Gado said. He said, “On Tuesday morning, we received a call from an unidentified telephone number. The caller demanded N2.5 million as ransom and informed us that the boy had been kidnapped.” According to him, “We agreed to pay the ransom because we wanted the boy to return home alive. We were hoping that he would be released, but what happened later shattered our hopes.” Gado said, “We were devastated when we received the news that his body had been found. It was a painful experience for the family because we had hoped to secure his release.” He added, “The boy’s body was reportedly discovered on Tuesday evening in a narrow passage near his family’s residence. The incident has thrown the family and residents of the neighbourhood into mourning.” Expressing concern over the killing, the uncle said, “We suspect that the people behind this incident may be familiar with the neighbourhood. We want security agencies to investigate the matter and ensure that those responsible are arrested.” He further said, “We are appealing to the security agencies to do everything possible to unravel the circumstances surrounding his death and bring the perpetrators to justice so that other families will not experience this kind of tragedy.” Efforts to obtain reactions from security operatives were unsuccessful as of press time. The post Suspected kidnappers kill 7-year-old boy hours after demanding N2.5m ransom in Jos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ebola: Senate Seeks Emergency Funding, Mandatory Screening At All Entry Points
item.description: The Senate has called on the Federal Government to provide emergency funding from the service-wide vote to strengthen the country’s disease surveillance system and enforce mandatory health screening at all international airports, seaports and designated land borders to prevent the spread of Ebola and other epidemic-prone diseases. The resolution followed a motion of urgent national importance sponsored by Senator Francis Faduyile, who raised concerns over the spread of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus and the risk it poses to Nigeria’s public health system. Faduyile noted that the outbreak, which began in the DRC, had spread to other African countries, including Uganda and Kenya, highlighting the risk of infected travellers entering Nigeria through third countries. He also cited the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention’s assessment of a high risk of Ebola importation, recalling that a single traveller brought the disease into Nigeria through Lagos in July 2014. ﻿ The Senate acknowledged the Federal Government’s existing measures, including the introduction of health declaration forms and enhanced screening at entry points. However, it expressed concern that screening requirements had been restricted to travellers from selected countries, potentially leaving gaps in the country’s surveillance system. Lawmakers also raised concerns over inadequate staffing and equipment at several entry points, as well as the continued reliance of Port Health Services on the Quarantine Act of 1926. The upper chamber warned that Nigeria’s existing disease burden, including Lassa fever, cholera and diphtheria, makes it imperative for the country to strengthen its preparedness against another major public health emergency. Consequently, the Senate asked the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the NCDC and Port Health Services to make health screening compulsory for all arriving international passengers, irrespective of nationality or country of departure. The proposed screening measures include health declaration forms, temperature checks and symptom assessments, with enhanced screening for travellers who have visited or transited through affected areas within the preceding 21 days. The Senate also called for exit screening for departing passengers during declared public health emergencies. It further urged the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria and the Nigeria Immigration Service to provide adequate numbers of trained Port Health officers, thermal scanners, protective equipment and isolation facilities at all entry points. The Federal Government was also urged to ensure that isolation and treatment centres are adequately prepared across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. On the legal framework, the Senate called for the replacement of the Quarantine Act of 1926 with a modern public health law aligned with the International Health Regulations of 2005. item.dc:creator: Alexander Okere
item.content:encoded: The Senate has called on the Federal Government to provide emergency funding from the service-wide vote to strengthen the country’s disease surveillance system and enforce mandatory health screening at all international airports, seaports and designated land borders to prevent the spread of Ebola and other epidemic-prone diseases. The resolution followed a motion of urgent national importance sponsored by Senator Francis Faduyile, who raised concerns over the spread of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus and the risk it poses to Nigeria’s public health system. Faduyile noted that the outbreak, which began in the DRC, had spread to other African countries, including Uganda and Kenya, highlighting the risk of infected travellers entering Nigeria through third countries. He also cited the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention’s assessment of a high risk of Ebola importation, recalling that a single traveller brought the disease into Nigeria through Lagos in July 2014. ﻿ The Senate acknowledged the Federal Government’s existing measures, including the introduction of health declaration forms and enhanced screening at entry points. However, it expressed concern that screening requirements had been restricted to travellers from selected countries, potentially leaving gaps in the country’s surveillance system. Lawmakers also raised concerns over inadequate staffing and equipment at several entry points, as well as the continued reliance of Port Health Services on the Quarantine Act of 1926. The upper chamber warned that Nigeria’s existing disease burden, including Lassa fever, cholera and diphtheria, makes it imperative for the country to strengthen its preparedness against another major public health emergency. Consequently, the Senate asked the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the NCDC and Port Health Services to make health screening compulsory for all arriving international passengers, irrespective of nationality or country of departure. The proposed screening measures include health declaration forms, temperature checks and symptom assessments, with enhanced screening for travellers who have visited or transited through affected areas within the preceding 21 days. The Senate also called for exit screening for departing passengers during declared public health emergencies. It further urged the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria and the Nigeria Immigration Service to provide adequate numbers of trained Port Health officers, thermal scanners, protective equipment and isolation facilities at all entry points. The Federal Government was also urged to ensure that isolation and treatment centres are adequately prepared across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. On the legal framework, the Senate called for the replacement of the Quarantine Act of 1926 with a modern public health law aligned with the International Health Regulations of 2005. It also urged the ministries of finance, budget, and economic planning to provide adequate funding for the NCDC and Port Health Services in the 2027 budget and release outstanding funds. Nigeria Confirms First Case On Wednesday, the Federal Government confirmed a case of the virus in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, said in Abuja that the imported case of Ebola virus disease was confirmed by laboratory testing. Pate noted that the patient is a woman with a recent travel history to Uganda, who returned to Nigeria with symptoms on October 7, which progressed four days later before tests confirmed the infection. However, the Ugandan authorities denied reports of an Ebola outbreak in the East African nation. Uganda’s Ministry of Health said that the location of exposure remains under investigation, adding that travel through Uganda alone was insufficient to establish where the infection occurred. It also stated that the Nigerian government had yet to provide detailed information about the patient’s travel itinerary and clinical history, which it said would help guide further investigations and any necessary contact tracing. The deadly viral haemorrhagic fever has spread to several countries across the continent since the outbreak in the DR Congo in May. Kenya reported its ninth Ebola case on Tuesday. The DRC’s Ebola epidemic has become the deadliest in the country’s history in several months, killing over 4,00 people out of more than 9,000 confirmed cases, according to health authorities. item.title: Spotify is busting free of CarPlay with the launch of its first native car app
item.description: Spotify announced Wednesday the launch of its next-generation, fully native in-car app, built directly on Google's Android Automotive operating system. The standalone app, which is launching today in select Audi models, runs directly on the vehicle's infotainment hardware - eliminating the need for phone tethering, Bluetooth connections, or aux cables. It's the clearest sign yet that Spotify is ready to move beyond Apple CarPlay and Android, popular phone projection systems that currently dominate the way most people consume media in their cars. item.title: I can’t get enough of the iPhone Duo’s matte inner display
item.description: Easy on the eyes. The iPhone Duo has all the messiness of a first-gen product . And while I'm not sure I love all of the decisions Apple made around its design, it got one thing right: the matte finish on the inner screen. I've been using it for the past week to watch movies on a plane, peruse my photo gallery, and catch up on a little reading, and I'm convinced. The matte screen is the best thing about the Duo, and I hope every other foldable maker copies it. item.title: The iPhone Duo is a messy, expensive, good time
item.description: The iPhone Duo is the riskiest Apple product in years. It's a huge rethink of what an iPhone is and could be, and it contains the seeds of many fascinating ideas that might be great in the future. But that future is yet to come. The iPhone Duo is also one of Apple's messiest first-generation products in a long time, and right now it will delight gadget nerds and early adopters and likely frustrate everyone else. It's been a minute since the iPhone has looked or worked significantly differently. item.title: AI has 'potential' to turn script kiddies into sophisticated infrastructure attackers
item.description: When it comes to cyberattacks that shut down power grids, drinking-water systems, and other critical infrastructure, AI doesn’t – yet – turn script kiddies into sophisticated, nation-state attackers. But “the potential is there,” according to operational technology (OT) security experts. "One thing that we've relied on for years is security by obscurity when it comes to utilities," said Steve Swick, former chief information security officer at American Electric Power. " The knowledge needed to do some of that stuff is getting less likely to be necessary," Swick added during a media panel ahead of the publication of Frenos' State of AI in Security report. AI makes it easier and faster for human attackers to target critical infrastructure , gain access to utilities and manufacturing plants, and perform OT system reconnaissance. “Basic access can recon documentation, and distill through that documentation very quickly to find out critical design features of your plant and facility,” said Paul Shaver, head of OT at Armadin, during the panel. “I can download the manual for almost any automation controller, parse through that very quickly, and come up with ways that I can exploit a dedicated feature of something that was not secure by design.” Armadin is Kevin Mandia’s new security startup that uses swarms of autonomous AI agents to simulate real-world cyberattacks . Prior to joining Armadin, Shaver spent six years as the global OT practice leader at Mandia’s earlier company, Mandiant, which Google acquired in 2022. “I will fly my Mandiant flag for a second and try to steer away from the fear, uncertainty, and death of the world is coming to an end, and every script kiddie is now a very sophisticated nation-state adversary. But I’m not going to say the potential is not there, because the tools are improving such that the access to information is so much quicker.” At Armadin, and with an AI assist, “I'm very quickly building tools in days that would normally have taken me months,” Shaver said. “If it can do that for me, it's doing something similar for the folks that have a very basic skill set. I wouldn't go so far as to script kiddies yet, but as the models improve, that becomes more of a possibility in this space.” Plus, as AI lowers the technical barriers to would-be OT hackers, “it advances the timeline,” said Harry Thomas, chief technology officer and co-founder of Frenos, a security company that does AI pentesting for OT environments. “If a better-than-average script kiddie can now perform attacks,” Thomas said, “You have more threat actors out there. item.dc:creator: Jessica Lyons
item.content:encoded: When it comes to cyberattacks that shut down power grids, drinking-water systems, and other critical infrastructure, AI doesn’t – yet – turn script kiddies into sophisticated, nation-state attackers. But “the potential is there,” according to operational technology (OT) security experts. "One thing that we've relied on for years is security by obscurity when it comes to utilities," said Steve Swick, former chief information security officer at American Electric Power. " The knowledge needed to do some of that stuff is getting less likely to be necessary," Swick added during a media panel ahead of the publication of Frenos' State of AI in Security report. AI makes it easier and faster for human attackers to target critical infrastructure , gain access to utilities and manufacturing plants, and perform OT system reconnaissance. “Basic access can recon documentation, and distill through that documentation very quickly to find out critical design features of your plant and facility,” said Paul Shaver, head of OT at Armadin, during the panel. “I can download the manual for almost any automation controller, parse through that very quickly, and come up with ways that I can exploit a dedicated feature of something that was not secure by design.” Armadin is Kevin Mandia’s new security startup that uses swarms of autonomous AI agents to simulate real-world cyberattacks . Prior to joining Armadin, Shaver spent six years as the global OT practice leader at Mandia’s earlier company, Mandiant, which Google acquired in 2022. “I will fly my Mandiant flag for a second and try to steer away from the fear, uncertainty, and death of the world is coming to an end, and every script kiddie is now a very sophisticated nation-state adversary. But I’m not going to say the potential is not there, because the tools are improving such that the access to information is so much quicker.” At Armadin, and with an AI assist, “I'm very quickly building tools in days that would normally have taken me months,” Shaver said. “If it can do that for me, it's doing something similar for the folks that have a very basic skill set. I wouldn't go so far as to script kiddies yet, but as the models improve, that becomes more of a possibility in this space.” Plus, as AI lowers the technical barriers to would-be OT hackers, “it advances the timeline,” said Harry Thomas, chief technology officer and co-founder of Frenos, a security company that does AI pentesting for OT environments. “If a better-than-average script kiddie can now perform attacks,” Thomas said, “You have more threat actors out there. There's an acceleration in timeline, more attacks could be happening, and from a defensive position, you might not know who your threat actor is anymore.” Testing the power of LLMs to help plan attacks The Frenos report, published Wednesday, examined the extent to which AI could help someone plan an attack on industrial systems. To do this, it ran several AI models through 16,980 tests between October 2025 and September 2026. These included 13,884 decision attempts, 2,520 planning attempts, and 576 simulated attacks. The company won’t disclose the models or providers’ names, but said it tested six frontier models, two US open weight models, and two foreign open weight models, on three kinds of tasks: choosing one action, planning the steps to a goal, and working through a simulated scenario. Each test gave the model background information and a set of attack actions to choose from. Before choosing, each model received details about assets, networks, and known weaknesses, plus the access each action required. Frenos then checked whether the model’s choice matched the required outcome. Depending on the model, between 6 percent and 47 percent of the choices passed. These tests found that the strongest three frontier models succeeded in about 90 percent of their planning attempts – meaning they produced a workable attack plan – but these same models weren’t consistent: 60 percent, 62.9 percent, and 74.3 percent of the attack plans passed every repeat. “A plan can look sensible and still leave out something essential,” according to the report. “The models had information about the task, but some answers skipped a step or assumed access that the plan had not established.” Meanwhile, the most successful of the four open weight models – a non-US model – achieved a 36.2 percent overall success rate. That figure, however, was still higher than the overall success rates of three other US frontier models, which scored 31.9 percent, 18.8 percent, and 17.9 percent, respectively. “We're seeing that even though AI models help us accelerate our tooling, accelerate our access and knowledge transfer, they are still prone to hallucinations – aka mistakes,” Thomas said. “We still think human judgment remains essential for these AI models to make the threat actors achieve whatever mission or goal they're trying to achieve.” In these tests, no humans asked the models to correct their plans, whereas in a real-life attack, a miscreant who understood the target could spot a gap in the AI’s plan, provide more information, and ask the model to revise its answer. “On top of that, when we were testing the AI models, we used a harness that was pretty simple: Here's some information. Here's the context. Give me an answer,” Thomas said. “A more capable harness could have given these AI models more of an edge.” Based on the findings, Frenos recommends actions for OT defenders to take, starting with a layered defense. This involves segmenting networks, limiting remote access and user permissions, and testing recovery steps. “We have our business continuity plans and disaster recovery plans for a reason,” Thomas said. “Let's execute them.” ®

item.title: Orionid meteor shower peaks tonight: Here's the best time to spot shooting stars
item.description: null Don't miss the Orionid meteor shower peak tonight (Oct. 21-22) as tiny shards of Halley's Comet collide with Earth's atmosphere to carve fiery streaks through the Autumn sky! But will the light cast by the waxing gibbous moon spoil the show? The Orionid meteor shower activity peaks when Earth travels through the densest section of the debris trail left by Comet 1P/Halley. The comet is currently racing back towards the sun ahead of its next visit to the inner solar system in 2061. Under perfect dark sky conditions 10 to 20 shooting stars could brighten the night sky each hour as the peak unfolds, according to NASA . However, the light cast by the waxing moon — just four days from being full — will likely reduce the number of visible meteors by hiding fainter Orionids from sight. Orionid shooting stars will appear to travel away from a point of origin, close to the red star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion , rising above the eastern horizon an hour before midnight for viewers in the U.S. When and where to see Orionid shooting stars this October Your best chance at spotting the fast-moving meteors will come in the hours before dawn on Oct. 22, after the moon has set and the radiant approaches its highest point in the night sky. It's best not to stare directly at the radiant, where the glowing meteor trails will be relatively short compared to those left by shooting stars that appear 45-90 degrees away from the bright star Betelgeuse, thanks to an effect known as foreshortening. How to measure distances in the night sky using nothing but your hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Try to travel away from city lights and allow 20-30 minutes for your eyes to adapt to the dark. Always make sure someone knows where you're going if you head somewhere remote to catch the shower and be sure to take a red light to ensure that you can find your way while also preserving your night vision! Editor's Note: If you would like to share your Orionid shooting star photos with Space.com's readers, then please send your image(s), along with your name, location and comments to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: 2027: Court dismisses suit seeking registration of new political party
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed a suit seeking to compel Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to register a political association as Wisdom Party (WP), 88 days to the 2027 presidential election. Justice James Omotosho, in a judgment, held that the plaintiff’s claim lacked merit and the suit had become academic. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the plaintiff, Chief Mrs Chinasa Nwekeke, had filed the suit as the pro tem National Chairman and on behalf of Wisdom Party, a political association seeking a registration as a party. Nwekeke, in the originating summons marked FHC//ABJ/CS/746/2026 filed on April 14 by her lawyer, Mark Agbo, had sued INEC as the sole defendant. The plaintiff sought a declaration that the political association, “Wisdom Party”, to which INEC did not object to its name, symbol, and logo after the expiration of 90 days via its letter of intent on Sept. 22. She sought a declaration that the establishment of INEC’s Fund pursuant to Section 3 (1) & (2) of the Electoral Act, 2022, upon which the totality of the expenditure of the commission is charged, and Section 75(6) of the Electoral Act, 2022, which empowered INEC at its discretion to fix an administrative fee as a precondition for processing an application for registration of a political party, is unreasonable, unwarranted, unjustified and inconsistent with Section 4 (1) of the Electoral Act, 2022. She sought a declaration that the failure of INEC in responding to the letter of intent of the plaintiff was deemed to be a no objection to the name, symbol and acronym of the plaintiff’s association. She also sought a declaration that the provision of Section 75 (6) of the Electoral Act, 2022, which provides for a separate source of funds in the form of a fee or levy on political associations for the performance of the constitutional function of registration of political parties, is inconsistent with Section 4 (1) (f) of the Electoral Act, 2022, and thus should be struck down by the court. Nwekeke further submitted that INEC’s failure in providing its account details to the plaintiff’s association for payment of the administrative fee was deemed to be a waiver and that it was meant to frustrate the application of the plaintiff’s association. She therefore prayed the court for an order directing the defendant to accept from the plaintiff’s association its application for registration as a political party. Besides, she sought a declaration that the application submitted pursuant to the relief above was proper. INEC, through its lawyer, Segun Bello, disagreed with the plaintiff’s submissions. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: The Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed a suit seeking to compel Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to register a political association as Wisdom Party (WP), 88 days to the 2027 presidential election. Justice James Omotosho, in a judgment, held that the plaintiff’s claim lacked merit and the suit had become academic. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the plaintiff, Chief Mrs Chinasa Nwekeke, had filed the suit as the pro tem National Chairman and on behalf of Wisdom Party, a political association seeking a registration as a party. Nwekeke, in the originating summons marked FHC//ABJ/CS/746/2026 filed on April 14 by her lawyer, Mark Agbo, had sued INEC as the sole defendant. The plaintiff sought a declaration that the political association, “Wisdom Party”, to which INEC did not object to its name, symbol, and logo after the expiration of 90 days via its letter of intent on Sept. 22. She sought a declaration that the establishment of INEC’s Fund pursuant to Section 3 (1) & (2) of the Electoral Act, 2022, upon which the totality of the expenditure of the commission is charged, and Section 75(6) of the Electoral Act, 2022, which empowered INEC at its discretion to fix an administrative fee as a precondition for processing an application for registration of a political party, is unreasonable, unwarranted, unjustified and inconsistent with Section 4 (1) of the Electoral Act, 2022. She sought a declaration that the failure of INEC in responding to the letter of intent of the plaintiff was deemed to be a no objection to the name, symbol and acronym of the plaintiff’s association. She also sought a declaration that the provision of Section 75 (6) of the Electoral Act, 2022, which provides for a separate source of funds in the form of a fee or levy on political associations for the performance of the constitutional function of registration of political parties, is inconsistent with Section 4 (1) (f) of the Electoral Act, 2022, and thus should be struck down by the court. Nwekeke further submitted that INEC’s failure in providing its account details to the plaintiff’s association for payment of the administrative fee was deemed to be a waiver and that it was meant to frustrate the application of the plaintiff’s association. She therefore prayed the court for an order directing the defendant to accept from the plaintiff’s association its application for registration as a political party. Besides, she sought a declaration that the application submitted pursuant to the relief above was proper. INEC, through its lawyer, Segun Bello, disagreed with the plaintiff’s submissions. The electoral umpire, in its counter affidavit, stated that the plaintiff’s letter of intent did not have a symbol of the party and that the general election is fixed for January 2027, which means that the court, granting the reliefs of the plaintiff, means that it would be required to file a formal application letter and it would be less than 12 months to the general election. The commission also submitted that the letter of intent written by the plaintiff’s association did not meet the requirements of the law, as it did not contain the symbol of the proposed political party, and thus it is void. It argued that since there was no valid letter of intent, the plaintiff’s association had no right to claim reliefs. INEC, therefore, urged the court to refuse the reliefs sought. Delivering the judgment, Justice Omotosho observed that from a cursory look at Section 3, especially Section 3 (2)(c), aids, grants or any other accruals are quite open-ended. “An accrual in accounting terms refers to revenues and expenses. “This means that revenues generated by the defendant can be paid into the Independent National Electoral Commission Fund. “The administrative fee being debated by the plaintiff is meant for the registration of political parties, and being a revenue accruing to the defendant, it can rightly be paid into the Fund. “Importantly, this also implies that the defendant is within its powers to demand administrative or processing fees, such as fees for the production and certification of the national voters register. “The fact that an institution receives funding from the Federation Account does not mean that it cannot generate funds or charge fees for some of its activities. “For instance, the judiciary receives funding from the Consolidated Revenue Fund; however, courts still fix filing fees and processing fees for court processes. “There is no express prohibition on the defendant to refrain from fixing administrative fees. “Consequently, I hold that the defendant has powers to fix administrative fees for the purpose of registration of political parties. “In final analysis, the claim of the plaintiff is without merit, and the suit has become academic. Consequently, the suit is hereby dismissed,” the judge ruled. (NAN) The post 2027: Court dismisses suit seeking registration of new political party appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ligue 1 game postponed as unrest grips France
item.description: The Ligue 1 match between Toulouse and Troyes this weekend has been pushed back a day at the request of local authorities struggling to contain unrest in France, the French league (LFP) announced on Wednesday. The match, which had been due to take place in Toulouse in southwest France at 1715 local time (1515 GMT) on Saturday, will now kick off on Sunday at the same time. “Although not considered high-risk, organising an event with such a large turnout requires the deployment of internal security forces and municipal police personnel,” the Haute-Garonne prefecture, which manages public services and security in the region, said. A second sporting event is also scheduled in Toulouse on Saturday, with the city’s rugby club set to host Perpignan in a Top 14 rugby match. On Tuesday, the Ligue 2 match between Montpellier and Paris-based Red Star originally scheduled for Saturday was moved to Monday. Some of the worst urban violence to hit France in years erupted last Saturday on the fringe of nationwide protests over the rising cost of living. Since then, authorities have ordered partial curfews in parts of Paris and other cities, including Toulouse, to prevent further violence. There was tight security at the Parc des Princes in Paris on Tuesday for Paris Saint-Germain’s victory against Barcelona in the Champions League. PSG will host Lyon at the same venue in a Ligue 1 match on Sunday evening. AFP The post Ligue 1 game postponed as unrest grips France appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Cross River Assembly passes State Police Bill
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Cross River State House of Assembly on Tuesday passed the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, endorsing the proposed establishment of state police to address insecurity through a decentralised policing system. All 22 lawmakers present at plenary voted in favour of the bill, with none opposing it. Three of the Assembly’s 25 members were absent during the vote. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria. It contains 26 clauses and proposes 25 alterations through substitutions to provisions of the principal Act, including Sections 84(4), 89(2), 121(3), 124(4), 109(2), 153(1), 157(2), 158(1) and 160. Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Elvert Ayambem, said the vote reflected the Assembly’s commitment to constitutional reforms aimed at addressing security challenges and protecting lives and property. “By this vote, the 10th Assembly has demonstrated its support for the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which seeks to establish a constitutional framework for State Police Services,” he said. Ayambem, however, stressed that the implementation of state policing must be guided by the rule of law, accountability and democratic principles. Contributing to the debate, the Leader of the House and member representing Odukpani State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Francis Asuquo, said policing must be brought closer to the people. He argued that a decentralised system would improve security responses and enable law enforcement agencies to address challenges peculiar to grassroots communities. The member representing Yala I State Constituency, Hon. Brian Odey, called for effective coordination between state and federal security agencies to ensure that the proposed State Police Services complemented existing security structures and improved overall operations. The Deputy Leader of the House and member representing Abi State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Davies Eta, emphasised the need for adequate safeguards, accountability and professionalism in the proposed system. He said state police must operate within the confines of the law and respect citizens’ fundamental rights. Lawmakers also identified improved intelligence gathering and better protection of lives and property as potential benefits of decentralised policing. The passage marks the Cross River Assembly’s endorsement of the proposed constitutional amendments. The bill must proceed through the constitutionally prescribed amendment process before the proposed changes can take effect nationally. item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is reveling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the NWSL, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: 2027: Police warn politicians against inflammatory speeches during campaigns
item.description: By Davies Iheamnachor The Commissioner of Police in Rivers State, Olugbenga Adepoju, has tasked political parties and their candidates for the 2027 elections to engage in issue-based campaigns and shun inflammatory rhetoric. This was as stakeholders, including party leaders, traditional rulers and civil society organisations, have called on political actors. security agencies and citizens to embrace peaceful conduct before, during and after the 2027 general elections. These calls formed the major discussions of the one-day Rivers Dialogue, organised by the newsroom of Megalectrics Limited, operators of Beat FM, Classic FM and Naija FM, in collaboration with the Professor Oke Onuchuku Institute of Peace and Conflict Studies, Ignatius Ajuru University of Education, Port Harcourt. The dialogue, themed “Peaceful Elections: Sustainable Path for Economic Development,” brought together political actors, traditional rulers and other stakeholders to discuss ways to prevent electoral violence and strengthen democracy in the 2027 polls. Addressing the participants, Adepoju said peaceful elections were necessary to sustain investors’ confidence, protect businesses and create an environment for development. Adepoju, who was represented by the Assistant Commissioner of Police (Operations) for the Rivers State Police Command, Ikechukwu Okoro, urged political parties to discourage violence among their supporters and advised candidates to focus on issue-based campaigns rather than inflammatory rhetoric. He further called on the media to use their platforms responsibly to promote peace rather than escalate tensions during the election. Meanwhile, Head of News Department, Megaletrics, Allwell Ene, said the dialogue was put together to ensure a violence free election in the state. He said: “The Rivers Dialogue was designed towards fostering violence-free and peaceful elections in Rivers State come 2027. Elections are critical periods in Nigeria because they alter the power structure within a state, the sub-national and the national levels where known political actors seek to establish their claims to power.” Ene noted that the state is notorious for electoral violence and security breaches during elections in the country, adding that such violence spills into other elections which subsequently paralyses governance and economic activities in the state; hence, the dialogue intends to address some of the issues. Also speaking, the Director-General of the National Orientation Agency, Mallam Lanre Issa-Onilu, said credible elections required the collective responsibility of citizens, political institutions and electoral stakeholders. Issa-Onilu, represented by the Rivers State Director of NOA, Dr Banigo Edward, said the increasing number of registered voters alone could not guarantee credible elections without civic discipline, active participation and responsible conduct before, during and after the polls. The dialogue, themed “Peaceful Elections: Sustainable Path for Economic Development,” brought together political actors, traditional rulers and other stakeholders to discuss ways to prevent electoral violence and strengthen democracy in the 2027 polls. Addressing the participants, Adepoju said peaceful elections were necessary to sustain investors’ confidence, protect businesses and create an environment for development. Adepoju, who was represented by the Assistant Commissioner of Police (Operations) for the Rivers State Police Command, Ikechukwu Okoro, urged political parties to discourage violence among their supporters and advised candidates to focus on issue-based campaigns rather than inflammatory rhetoric. He further called on the media to use their platforms responsibly to promote peace rather than escalate tensions during the election. Meanwhile, Head of News Department, Megaletrics, Allwell Ene, said the dialogue was put together to ensure a violence free election in the state. He said: “The Rivers Dialogue was designed towards fostering violence-free and peaceful elections in Rivers State come 2027. Elections are critical periods in Nigeria because they alter the power structure within a state, the sub-national and the national levels where known political actors seek to establish their claims to power.” Ene noted that the state is notorious for electoral violence and security breaches during elections in the country, adding that such violence spills into other elections which subsequently paralyses governance and economic activities in the state; hence, the dialogue intends to address some of the issues. Also speaking, the Director-General of the National Orientation Agency, Mallam Lanre Issa-Onilu, said credible elections required the collective responsibility of citizens, political institutions and electoral stakeholders. Issa-Onilu, represented by the Rivers State Director of NOA, Dr Banigo Edward, said the increasing number of registered voters alone could not guarantee credible elections without civic discipline, active participation and responsible conduct before, during and after the polls. He said: “A free, fair and credible election in 2027 cannot be guaranteed by INEC alone. It requires a collective responsibility, civic discipline, moral courage and active participation of every citizen.” However, the Paramount Ruler of Elelenwo Etor Kingdom in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of the state, His Royal Highness, Eze Sunny Weli Chukwu, called for proper training and orientation for security personnel deployed for election monitoring to prevent unnecessary violence. Chukwu urged the Independent National Electoral Commission to ensure eligible voters had access to their Permanent Voter Cards and called on traditional rulers to educate their communities, particularly youths, against electoral violence and vote-buying. Meanwhile, the All Progressives Congress governorship candidate in Rivers State, Hon. Kingsley Ogundu Chinda, pledged his commitment to peaceful elections and governance, emphasising that protecting lives and property remained the primary responsibility of government. He said, “I am fully, unconditionally committed to a peaceful election and peaceful governance in Rivers State.” Other governorship candidates, including those of the Social Democratic Party and the Peoples Redemption Party, National Rescue Movement as well as Boot, also expressed their commitment to non-violent elections in the state. item.title: Nvidia picks OpenShell to tame AI gents
item.description: Nvidia has proposed a new way to keep corporate AI agents in line. Nvidia on Wednesday introduced its OpenShell Reference Architecture . Based on the company's OpenShell secure runtime, It's a recipe for creating, operating, observing, and policing AI agents using OpenShell on Nvidia hardware. "Nvidia created OpenShell to give agents the freedom to do useful work within clearly defined boundaries — contained, monitored and under control," CEO Jensen Huang said in a canned statement. "With the OpenShell Reference Architecture, agents can think on Rubin, act on Vera and be governed on BlueField." AI agents are touted as a powerful automation technology. The reality is that they can be unruly, as demonstrated by security testing OpenAI and Anthropic conducted, during which their models exceeded their remit and attacked third-party organizations. Developers of existing agents, like Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, and OpenCode, therefore include controls that limit access to tools like curl and bash. Devs also create sandboxes to isolate an agentic process from the host, so that if agents go awry they're contained. OpenShell sits a level above that with a runtime that extends sandboxing to govern gateway-brokered credentials, identity and policy boundaries, and (eventually) routing and workflows too. At least mostly – OpenShell still has a few open security-related issues listed on GitHub. To implement OpenShell, organizations need Nvidia hardware. The company's blueprint calls for Nvidia Vera Rubin infrastructure to run models like Nvidia Nemotron, with agent harnesses handled via Vera CPUs, and Nvidia BlueField-4 DPUs (aka SmartNICs) propping up Nvidia Sentry security software to monitor agent behavior. The AI biz has made this blueprint available to partners capable of powering Linux and Kubernetes infrastructure. The usual suspects are aboard: Canonical, SUSE and Red Hat. Cloud hyperscalers Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure have also been tapped as vendors for this vision. And of course Nvidia's floor plan applies to agents from various model builders, including Anthropic, Cohere, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Perplexity, Reflection, and SpaceX. Nvidia says several banks – Europe’s BBVA and Santander – are perusing the OpenShell Reference Architecture spec to see how it aligns with their security and governance requirements. And the AI biz is not too modest to let slip that SAP is integrating the OpenShell Reference Architecture with its Joule Studio runtime for safer agent operations. It's worth noting that OpenShell collects telemetry data by default, "to improve the project," Nvidia insists. The biz allows users to opt-out, with a cautionary note: "Third-party services, model providers, inference endpoints, agents, or tools that you configure and use with OpenShell may have their own terms and privacy practices." ®

item.title: Nvidia's grand plan for speeding up datacenter deployments: AI trailer parks
item.description: Datacenters are taking too long to bring online to fill the demand of the AI boom. So starting in 2027, Nvidia and its partners will offer its Vera Rubin rack systems fully plumbed, wired, and ready for deployment in modular bit barns. The containers, which Nvidia calls DSX pods, were unveiled at GTC Berlin this week and are essentially the datacenter equivalent of a trailer home. Built by partners like HPE, Dell, Schneider Electric, and others, each DSX pod will come fully furnished with all the compute, interconnects, electrical, and plumbing a growing AI factory might need. Just drop the pod on a prepared datacenter site, hook up power, networking, and cooling, and you'll be churning out tokens and raking in profit in no time. Or that's Nvidia's sales pitch anyway. Inside the 28 metric ton containers you'll find seven Vera Rubin NVL72 racks packing 504 GPUs and 252 Vera CPUs. GPUzilla says the pods will cut datacenter deployment times from six months to as little as two weeks because it will validate every fitting, cable, and component before it leaves the factory. The idea being if there is something wrong, it'll get caught there rather than after customers have gone through the trouble of hooking everything up. And just like a trailer home, Nvidia's DSX pods will be entirely customizable. Prefer HPE over Dell, or Eaton over Schneider? No problem, Nvidia has roped all its buddies into building these compute containers. And if you ever need more compute, just add another trailer and you've got yourself a double wide, which will surely be the envy of all your neocloud neighbors. The first DSX pods powered by Nvidia's Vera Rubin rack systems should roll off the production line early next year, and reflect the company's ongoing effort to quash supply chain challenges before they start eating into revenues. Also at GTC Berlin, Nvidia laid out out new DSX specs for waterless datacenters, which use closed loop coolants and dry coolers rather than water-thirsty cooling towers. This effort builds on work announced at the AI Infra Summit earlier this year, when Nvidia touted its effeorts to squeeze more performance out of less juice , while also allowing bit barns to spin down their workloads in response to changing grid conditions. ®

item.title: Uganda denies Ebola outbreak after Nigeria confirms imported case
item.description: Uganda has denied having an active Ebola outbreak following Nigeria’s confirmation of an imported case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), insisting that it has no confirmed active infections as authorities investigate where the patient contracted the virus. In a public statement issued in Kampala on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, Uganda’s Ministry of Health said the Nigerian patient had travelled through the country before arriving in Nigeria but stressed that her transit did not establish where she was infected. “We wish to clarify that, as at the time of this statement, Uganda has NO confirmed active Ebola cases,” the ministry said. The statement, titled “Reported Ebola Case in Nigeria: We Call for Calm and Vigilance,” added that preliminary information indicated the woman had travelled through Uganda in early October without symptoms and developed them after arriving in Nigeria. “Travel through Uganda does not establish that infection occurred here. The location of exposure remains under investigation,” the ministry said. It added that Nigeria’s government was expected to provide detailed information about the woman’s travel itinerary and clinical history to support further investigations and any necessary contact tracing. The Ugandan authorities also said they were strengthening screening and public health controls at points of entry in collaboration with relevant agencies. Nigeria’s Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, announced the confirmed case on Tuesday, saying laboratory tests had established that the woman was infected with Ebola virus disease. According to Pate, the patient had recently travelled to East Africa, including Uganda, before returning to Nigeria with symptoms on October 7. Her condition reportedly worsened four days later, prompting further medical attention and testing. The woman was admitted to a private hospital, where she received treatment for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed. She has since been isolated and is receiving medical care. Pate said health authorities had identified 44 contacts and commenced contact tracing to prevent further transmission. Surveillance has also been strengthened at Nigeria’s points of entry. The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare is coordinating the response with the FCT Health Services Secretariat, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention and other public health partners. The minister urged public and private healthcare facilities to remain vigilant and maintain a high index of suspicion for possible Ebola cases, particularly among patients with relevant travel histories and compatible symptoms. He also urged Nigerians to remain calm, practise good hygiene and promptly seek medical attention if they experience symptoms such as fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea. item.title: NBTI announces $600m pipeline for Nigerian innovation
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The National Board for Technology Incubation (NBTI) has unveiled an investment and development-finance pipeline exceeding $600 million for solar energy and other development initiatives, following the participation of 298 Nigerian innovators at the NextGen Innovation Challenge 2026 in London. The proposed financing comprises a $500 million solar-energy programme for universities and polytechnics and a $100 million financing arrangement for the Tinubu Light Initiative. The funds, however, have not been confirmed as received or fully mobilised. Speaking at a world press conference on Wednesday, NBTI Director-General, Dr Kazeem Kolawole Raji, said the October 9 event, organised in partnership with UKALD, provided an international platform for showcasing Nigerian technologies and connecting innovators with investors and commercial partners. The number of participating innovators rose from 105 in 2025 to 298 this year, representing all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with innovations spanning agriculture, healthcare, artificial intelligence, renewable energy and advanced manufacturing. “Our innovators have demonstrated that Nigeria has ideas worthy of international attention. Our responsibility is to help create the conditions in which those ideas can grow, compete and deliver lasting value to our people,” Raji said. NBTI said discussions with Gigawatt Global focused on developing solar farms in universities and polytechnics under power purchase agreements, while a memorandum of understanding with Financial Innovation for Impact, UK, also known as Cambridge Investors, covered the proposed $100 million financing for the Tinubu Light Initiative. The initiative targets one million micro and small businesses for solar-energy solutions, 50,000 direct youth jobs and 10,000 trained field marketers, with ₦30 billion in blended financing targeted for its first phase. Other outcomes include an announced $100,000 investment commitment by Dubai-based investor Erin Grover for three women innovators and international acceleration opportunities valued at $160,000 for 16 selected innovators. The Learning and Development Bureau UK also offered leadership and management scholarships worth more than £80,000 collectively to the 16 innovators and pledged assistance with UK Global Talent Visa applications, subject to eligibility. Raji said the priority was now to turn the opportunities into viable businesses, jobs and measurable economic benefits, urging investors and development partners to support Nigerian innovators with funding, mentorship and market access. “Our focus must now move decisively from visibility to implementation, from promising concepts to commercially viable solutions, and from announcements to independently verifiable outcomes,” he said. The post NBTI announces $600m pipeline for Nigerian innovation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PANDEF mourns Uduaghan, hails his peacebuilding role
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, has mourned the death of former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan, who died three days before his 72nd birthday, according to his family. PANDEF National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, described Uduaghan as an exceptional leader whose commitment to the people of Delta State was unwavering. Igali stated this in a condolence letter to Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, on the death of the former governor, according to a statement issued on Wednesday. He praised Uduaghan for his significant contributions to peace and stability in the Niger Delta, particularly during his tenure as Secretary to the State Government and later as governor, when militancy was heightened across the region. In the letter, Igali said he was shocked by the news of Uduaghan’s death, describing the late governor as a close associate and personal friend. “I write to express my total shock at the news of the passing into glory of our dearly beloved brother, the former Governor of Delta State, HE Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan. Although we mourn, but we all hold strong belief that the Almighty God knows best, and we glorify His exalted name,” he said. Igali added that he and Uduaghan had maintained a cordial relationship since they served simultaneously as secretaries to their respective state governments. “Without doubt, he was an exceptional man through and through, whose commitment to the people of Delta State was unfettered,” he said. He noted that Uduaghan played a significant role in bringing peace and stability to the Niger Delta during a period of heightened militancy in the South-South region. Igali described the former governor’s death as a major loss not only to Delta State but also to the Niger Delta and Nigeria as a whole. He expressed hope that Uduaghan’s legacy of service to God and humanity would endure, saying the late governor had “embedded his name in gold in the annals of our history.” Igali also asked Oborevwori to convey his deepest condolences to the Uduaghan family and the people of Delta State, praying for the repose of the former governor’s soul. The post PANDEF mourns Uduaghan, hails his peacebuilding role appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Showunmi reaffirms commitment to Abiola’s legacy, national unity
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Convener of the Alternative Movement, Otunba Segun Showunmi has reaffirmed his commitment to Nigeria’s unity, democratic development and the ideals for which the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale (MKO) Abiola sacrificed his life, insisting that the struggle to actualise the June 12, 1993 presidential election mandate remains a defining moment in his political journey. Showunmi, in a statement titled “My Scar from MKO Abiola, My Sacrifice for Democracy, and My Unwavering Pan-Nigerian Conviction,” said the circumstances surrounding Abiola’s death and the annulment of the historic election had left an indelible mark on his life and political convictions. He also cautioned political actors against actions capable of undermining national stability, particularly the premature or unauthorised announcement of election results in ways that could trigger political tension and plunge the country into chaos. “The scar in my heart from the loss of Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola has not fully healed,” Showunmi said, adding that he would neither trivialise Abiola’s sacrifice nor pretend to be unfamiliar with the painful experiences that shaped Nigeria’s democratic struggle. He stressed that his remarks on the country’s political history had been misunderstood by some people, insisting that his intention was to caution against political conduct that could endanger peace, violate the law or destabilise the nation. item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Convener of the Alternative Movement, Otunba Segun Showunmi has reaffirmed his commitment to Nigeria’s unity, democratic development and the ideals for which the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale (MKO) Abiola sacrificed his life, insisting that the struggle to actualise the June 12, 1993 presidential election mandate remains a defining moment in his political journey. Showunmi, in a statement titled “My Scar from MKO Abiola, My Sacrifice for Democracy, and My Unwavering Pan-Nigerian Conviction,” said the circumstances surrounding Abiola’s death and the annulment of the historic election had left an indelible mark on his life and political convictions. He also cautioned political actors against actions capable of undermining national stability, particularly the premature or unauthorised announcement of election results in ways that could trigger political tension and plunge the country into chaos. “The scar in my heart from the loss of Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola has not fully healed,” Showunmi said, adding that he would neither trivialise Abiola’s sacrifice nor pretend to be unfamiliar with the painful experiences that shaped Nigeria’s democratic struggle. He stressed that his remarks on the country’s political history had been misunderstood by some people, insisting that his intention was to caution against political conduct that could endanger peace, violate the law or destabilise the nation. Showunmi said his reference to the political events of 1992 was intended to illustrate the consequences of abandoning caution, restraint and respect for the law in the pursuit of political power. “I invoked the events of 1992 to illustrate how political situations can spiral out of control when caution, restraint and respect for the law are abandoned,” he said. He maintained that his intervention was intended as a warning about the potential consequences of political decisions, not an endorsement of reckless conduct. “My intervention was a warning about consequences, not an invitation to recklessness, and I will not permit reactionary forces to turn my counsel into something it was never intended to be,” he stated. According to him, political advice should be offered in the national interest, while individuals must ultimately decide whether to heed such counsel. He urged political contestants to consider the wider implications of their actions, warning that decisions taken without regard for the law and national stability could have far-reaching consequences for the country. Reaffirming his commitment to national unity, Showunmi declared that his political convictions were not driven by ethnic considerations and rejected any suggestion that he subscribed to the superiority of one ethnic group over another. “I must also state, unequivocally, that I am a Pan-Nigerian through and through. I have no interest in promoting the idea that one ethnic group is superior to another,” he said. He explained that his political philosophy was rooted in the collective dignity, security and prosperity of Nigerians, irrespective of their ethnic or regional backgrounds. Showunmi urged Yoruba activists and others who might disagree with his position to consider his statements within the broader context of his commitment to Nigeria’s unity. “My words and actions must be understood within the framework of my commitment to the Nigerian nation. I will not subordinate that commitment to ethnic sentiment, sectional advantage or the politics of exclusion,” he said. He added that his preference for national cohesion should not be interpreted as a lack of personal conviction or an inadequate understanding of the country’s political history. On Nigeria’s political future, Showunmi reiterated his support for a power-sharing arrangement under which the presidency would rotate between the northern and southern parts of the country. He argued that a predictable and mutually respected understanding of power rotation could help reduce political suspicion, strengthen national cohesion and promote democratic stability. “I have long expressed the view that Nigeria should manage political power through a pendulum arrangement between the Northern and Southern parts of the country,” he said. “In my considered opinion, a predictable and mutually respected understanding of power rotation offers a framework for reducing suspicion, strengthening national cohesion and sustaining our democratic journey.” He described the proposal as part of the broader need for political maturity, mutual understanding and an inclusive approach to managing Nigeria’s diversity. Paying tribute to Abiola, the presumed winner of the June 12, 1993 presidential election, which was annulled by the military government, Showunmi said the late politician’s legacy remained inseparable from Nigeria’s struggle for democratic governance. He prayed that Abiola’s sacrifice would continue to inspire Nigerians to work towards a more stable, just and enduring democracy. “May your supreme sacrifice continue to guide Nigeria towards a more stable, just and enduring democracy. May the promise for which you paid such a terrible price never be betrayed,” he said. Showunmi also disclosed that he intended to speak more extensively in the future about his personal contributions to the pro-democracy struggle and how the events surrounding Abiola shaped his political trajectory. “One day, God willing, I will speak more fully about my own contributions to the struggle for democracy,” he said. According to him, the experiences surrounding Abiola and the struggle to reclaim the June 12 mandate influenced his political outlook and redirected the course of his life, setting in motion developments whose consequences he said were still unfolding. He also acknowledged the role played by media entrepreneur and publisher Dele Momodu during that period, describing his contribution as significant to that chapter of Nigeria’s political history. “I must also acknowledge Dele Momodu. May God spare his life. He played a key and pivotal role in that chapter of our history, and his contribution deserves to be remembered,” Showunmi said. Showunmi warned against interpreting his restraint as a lack of knowledge of Nigeria’s democratic history or mistaking his commitment to national unity for an absence of personal convictions. “Finally, let nobody mistake my restraint for ignorance of history or my commitment to national unity for an absence of personal conviction,” he said. He added: “My commitment is to Nigeria. My loyalty is to the democratic ideal. My respect for MKO Abiola’s sacrifice is enduring. And my conviction that Nigeria must survive, mature and prosper remains unshaken.” “May God bless Nigeria and all who genuinely labour for her progress,” he said. The post Showunmi reaffirms commitment to Abiola’s legacy, national unity appeared first on Vanguard News .
